title.zh: 卷446 列傳二百三十三 郭嵩焘弟：昆焘 崇厚 曾纪泽 薛福成 黎庶昌 马建忠 李凤苞 洪钧 刘瑞芬 徐寿朋 杨儒
title.en: Volume 446 Biographies 233: Guo Songdao younger brother: Kun Dao, Chong Hou, Ceng Jize, Xue Fucheng, Li Shuchang, Ma Jianzhong, Li Fengbao, Hong Jun, Liu Ruifen, Xu Shoupeng, Yang Ru
title.raw: 卷446 列傳二百三十三 郭嵩焘弟：昆焘 崇厚 曾纪泽 薛福成 黎庶昌 马建忠 李凤苞 洪钧 刘瑞芬 徐寿朋 杨儒

sentences.zh: 列傳二百三十三

translations.literal: Biographies, number two hundred thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 233

sentences.zh: 郭嵩燾弟昆燾崇厚曾紀澤薛福成黎庶昌馬建忠

translations.literal: Guo Songshen; his younger brothers Kunzhen and Chonghou; Zeng Jize; Xue Fucheng; Li Shuchang; Ma Jianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songshen, with his younger brothers Kunzhen and Chonghou; Zeng Jize; Xue Fucheng; Li Shuchang; and Ma Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 李鳳苞洪鈞劉瑞芬徐壽朋楊儒

translations.literal: Li Fengbao, Hong Jun, Liu Ruifen, Xu Shoupeng, Yang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengbao, Hong Jun, Liu Ruifen, Xu Shoupeng, and Yang Ru.

sentences.zh: 郭嵩燾，字筠仙，湖南湘陰人。

translations.literal: Guo Songshen, style name Yunxian, was a native of Xiangyin in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songshen, courtesy name Yunxian, came from Xiangyin in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，選庶吉士，遭憂歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and returned home upon bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1847, entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationer, and went home to observe mourning when a parent died.

sentences.zh: 會粵寇犯長沙，曾國藩奉詔治軍，嵩燾力讚之出。

translations.literal: Just then the Cantonese rebels attacked Changsha; Zeng Guofan received an edict to raise an army, and Songshen strongly urged him to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebels threatened Changsha, Zeng Guofan was ordered to organize troops, and Songshen pressed him hard to answer the call.

sentences.zh: 贛事亟，江忠源乞師國藩，國藩遣之往，從忠源守章門。

translations.literal: The situation in Gan was urgent; Jiang Zhongyuan begged Guofan for reinforcements, and Guofan sent Songshen there to follow Zhongyuan in defending Zhangmen.
translations.idiomatic: With Gan province in crisis, Jiang Zhongyuan asked Zeng Guofan for aid; Guofan sent Songshen to join Zhongyuan in holding Zhangmen.

sentences.zh: 是時寇艎集饒、瑞，分泊長江，因獻編練水師議，忠源韙之，令具疏請敕湖南北、四川制戰艦百餘艘。

translations.literal: At that time rebel war-junks gathered at Rao and Rui and anchored along the Yangtze in detachments; he therefore submitted a plan to organize and train a river fleet. Zhongyuan approved it and had him draft a memorial requesting an edict for Hunan, Hubei, and Sichuan to build more than a hundred warships.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel vessels then clustered at Rao and Rui and fanned out along the Yangtze. Songshen proposed raising a trained river navy; Zhongyuan agreed and told him to memorialize the throne for orders that Hunan, Hubei, and Sichuan build over a hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 嗣以贛被圍久，船非可剋期造，乃先造巨筏，列砲其上，與陸師夾擊，寇引去。

translations.literal: Later, because Gan had been besieged so long that ships could not be built on schedule, they first built huge rafts, mounted cannon on them, and attacked from both land and water; the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Gan’s long siege made warships impossible to finish in time, so they built great rafts instead, mounted guns on them, and struck the rebels from land and water together until the enemy drew off.

sentences.zh: 厥後用以塞湖口者即此筏也。

translations.literal: The rafts later used to block Hukou were these very ones.
translations.idiomatic: The same rafts were later used to block Hukou on Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 湘軍名大顯。

translations.literal: The fame of the Hunan Army became greatly manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan Army’s reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 論功，授編修。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 還朝，入直上書房。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he entered the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he joined the emperor’s Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，英人犯津沽，僧格林沁撤北塘備，嵩燾力​​爭之，議不合，辭去。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng the English attacked Taku; Sengge Rinchen withdrew the Beitang defenses, and Songshen argued strenuously against it; when opinion did not agree, he resigned.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when British forces struck Taku, Sengge Rinchen pulled back the Beitang garrison. Songshen fought the decision bitterly; unable to prevail, he quit his post.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，起授蘇松糧儲道，遷兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Tongzhi he was recalled and appointed grain intendant of Suzhou and Songjiang, then transferred to salt transport commissioner of the Liang-Huai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi came to the throne he was recalled, first as Suzhou–Songjiang grain intendant, then as Liang-Huai salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庫儲竭，諸軍仰餔淮鹺者數十萬，嵩燾躬自掣驗，配置各營。

translations.literal: The treasury was exhausted, and several hundred thousand troops depended on Huai salt for provisions; Songshen personally inspected and allocated supplies to each camp.
translations.idiomatic: With the coffers empty and hundreds of thousands of soldiers relying on Huai salt revenue, he personally inspected shipments and rationed each camp.

sentences.zh: 提督李世忠擁重兵行私鹺，亡誰何，益遣入捕治之，運政乃鬯。

translations.literal: Provincial commander Li Shizhong, holding heavy forces, trafficked in private salt with impunity; Songshen further sent men in to arrest and punish him, and only then did salt administration run smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commander Li Shizhong used his troops to run contraband salt with no one daring to stop him. Songshen sent officers to seize and punish him, and the salt trade finally settled down.

sentences.zh: 明年，署廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: The next year he served as acting governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he acted as Guangdong governor.

sentences.zh: 寇偪陽山，亟使張運蘭擊卻之。

translations.literal: Rebels pressed Yangshan; he urgently sent Zhang Yunlan to strike and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels threatened Yangshan, he quickly sent Zhang Yunlan to beat them back.

sentences.zh: 詔安陷，饒平、大埔警，與總督瑞麟遣將防邊，追入詔安城，殺數千人，軍稍振。

translations.literal: Zhao'an fell and Raoping and Dapu were alarmed; with Governor Rui Lin he dispatched generals to guard the border, pursued into Zhao'an city, killed several thousand men, and the army recovered somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhao'an fell and Raoping and Dapu came under threat, he and Governor Rui Lin sent generals to secure the frontier, drove the enemy back into Zhao'an, killed thousands, and morale improved.

sentences.zh: 是時金陵克，罷釐捐議起，嵩燾陳說利害凡千餘言，事遂寢。

translations.literal: At that time Jinling had been taken and debate arose over abolishing the transit levy; Songshen set forth advantages and disadvantages in more than a thousand words, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had just fallen, and officials debated ending the transit tax. Songshen wrote more than a thousand characters on the pros and cons, and the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 偽森王侯玉山避匿香港，恃英為護符，官吏莫能捕。

translations.literal: The false Sen King Hou Yushan hid in Hong Kong, relying on the English as a talisman, and officials could not seize him.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping prince Hou Yushan took refuge in Hong Kong under British protection, and local officials could not touch him.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾援公法與爭，執以歸，論斬。

translations.literal: Songshen cited international law in dispute, took him into custody and brought him back, and he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Songshen invoked international law, secured his extradition, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 而瑞麟遽張其功，以率兵往捕聞，嵩燾力止之，不可。

translations.literal: But Rui Lin hastily trumpeted the achievement, spreading word that he had led troops to capture the man; Songshen tried hard to stop it but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Lin then boasted that he had led troops to make the arrest. Songshen protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 英人大恚，數移牒詰責。

translations.literal: The English were greatly enraged and repeatedly sent notes of protest.
translations.idiomatic: The British were furious and sent repeated diplomatic protests.

sentences.zh: 初，毛鴻賓督粵，事皆決於幕僚徐灝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mao Hongbin governed Guangdong, all affairs were decided by his staff member Xu Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mao Hongbin’s governorship of Guangdong, staff secretary Xu Hao had run everything.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟繼至，灝益橫。

translations.literal: When Rui Lin succeeded him, Hao became still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui Lin took over, Xu Hao grew even more domineering.

sentences.zh: 嵩壽銜之，上疏論軍情數誤，劾逐灝，並自請罷斥。

translations.literal: Songshen harbored resentment, memorialized that military intelligence had repeatedly erred, impeached and demanded Hao’s expulsion, and also asked to be dismissed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Songshen, bitter over the affair, memorialized that military reports had repeatedly been wrong, demanded Xu Hao’s removal, and asked to be dismissed himself.

sentences.zh: 事下左宗棠，宗棠言其跡近負氣，被訶責。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Zuo Zongtang, who said his conduct smacked of petulance, and he was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to Zuo Zongtang, who said Songshen had acted out of pique; the court scolded him.

sentences.zh: 左、郭本姻家。

translations.literal: Zuo and Guo were originally related by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo and the Guo family were connected by marriage.

sentences.zh: 宗棠先厄於官文，罪不測，嵩燾為求解肅順，並言於同列潘祖廕，白無他，始獲免，至是宗棠竟不為疏辨。

translations.literal: Zongtang had earlier been imperiled by Guanwen and faced uncertain punishment; Songshen sought release through Sushun and also spoke to his colleague Pan Zuyin to clear him of other charges, so that he was first spared; yet now Zongtang would not plead for him in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Years before, when Guanwen had nearly ruined Zongtang, Songshen had appealed to Sushun and persuaded Pan Zuyin to vouch for him until he was cleared. Now Zongtang refused to speak up for him.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾念事皆繇督撫同城所誤，逾歲解職，遂上疏極論其弊，不報。

translations.literal: Songshen reflected that affairs had all been mistaken because governor-general and governor shared the same city; after more than a year he left office and then memorialized at length on the evils, without response.
translations.idiomatic: Songshen believed the trouble came from governor-general and governor sharing one city. A year after leaving office he submitted a long critique of that system, but the court never answered.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授福建按察使，未上，命直總署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed Fujian provincial judge, but before taking up the post was ordered to serve at the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he was named Fujian provincial judge, but before reporting he was assigned to the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部侍郎、出使英國大臣，兼使法。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of war and minister plenipotentiary to Britain, with concurrent mission to France.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war and appointed envoy to Britain, with concurrent accreditation to France.

sentences.zh: 英人馬加理入滇邊遇害，嵩燾疏劾岑毓英，意在朝廷自罷其職，藉箝外人口也。

translations.literal: The Englishman Margary was killed on entering the Yunnan border; Songshen memorialized impeaching Cen Yuying, intending that the court itself dismiss his own post so as to restrain foreign tongues.
translations.idiomatic: After the British interpreter Margary was killed on the Yunnan frontier, Songshen impeached Cen Yuying, hoping the court would recall him so foreign powers could not blame China for inaction.

sentences.zh: 而一時士論大譁，謂嵩燾媚外。

translations.literal: But opinion among scholars at the time was greatly agitated, saying Songshen fawned on foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion erupted, accusing Songshen of groveling to foreigners.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾言既不用，英使威妥瑪出都，邦交幾裂。

translations.literal: Songshen’s words were not adopted; the British minister Wade left the capital, and relations nearly broke.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ignored Songshen’s advice, British minister Wade quit Beijing and the alliance nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾又欲以身任之，上言：「交涉之方，不外理、勢。

translations.literal: Songshen again wished to take the burden on himself and submitted: "The methods of negotiation are nothing beyond principle and leverage.
translations.idiomatic: Songshen offered to shoulder the crisis himself and wrote: "Diplomacy rests on nothing but right and leverage.

sentences.zh: 勢者人與我共，可者與，不可者拒。

translations.literal: Leverage is what others share with me: what is acceptable, grant; what is not, refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Leverage is what others and we share in common: accept what we can, refuse what we cannot.

sentences.zh: 理者所以自處。

translations.literal: Principle is how one conducts oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Principle is how we conduct ourselves.

sentences.zh: 勢足而理直，固不可違；

translations.literal: When leverage is sufficient and principle is straight, it certainly cannot be violated;
translations.idiomatic: When leverage is strong and our case is just, we must not yield;

sentences.zh: 勢不足而別無可恃，尤恃理以折。」

translations.literal: when leverage is insufficient and there is nothing else to rely on, one especially depends on principle to prevail."
translations.idiomatic: when leverage fails and we have nothing else to lean on, we must rely all the more on principle to win the argument."

sentences.zh: 因條列四事以進。

translations.literal: He then itemized four points and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid out four proposals for the throne.

sentences.zh: 而郎中劉錫鴻者，方謀隨嵩燾出使，慮疏上觸忌，遏之，比嵩燾覺，始補上，而事已無及。

translations.literal: But the bureau director Liu Xihong, who was scheming to accompany Songshen abroad, feared the memorial would give offense and suppressed it; by the time Songshen discovered it and finally submitted a supplement, the affair was already beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau director Liu Xihong, who hoped to join Songshen’s mission, feared the memorial would offend the court and blocked it. Songshen only learned of this later and filed a belated copy, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 既蒞英，錫鴻為副使，益事事齮齕之，嵩燾不能堪，乞病歸，主講城南書院。

translations.literal: After he had arrived in Britain, Xihong served as deputy minister and increasingly obstructed him in every matter; Songshen could not endure it, begged leave on grounds of illness, returned home, and lectured at Chengnan Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Britain, with Xihong as deputy, the harassment grew constant. Songshen resigned on grounds of illness, came home, and taught at Chengnan Academy in Changsha.

sentences.zh: 未幾，而俄事棘。

translations.literal: Before long the Russian affair became acute.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the crisis with Russia sharpened.

sentences.zh: 崇厚以辱國論死，群臣多主戰，徵調騷然。

translations.literal: Chonghou was sentenced to death for disgracing the state; many ministers at court favored war, and mobilization caused widespread alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou faced execution for humiliating the nation; most courtiers wanted war, and mobilization threw the country into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾於是條上六事：曰收還伊犁，歸甘督覈議；

translations.literal: Songshen thereupon submitted six items in order: first, recovering Ili should be referred to the Gansu governor-general for verification;
translations.idiomatic: Songshen then submitted six recommendations: that recovery of Ili be reviewed by the Gansu governor-general;

sentences.zh: 曰遣使議還伊犁，當赴伊會辦；

translations.literal: second, envoys sent to negotiate the return of Ili should go to Ili to conduct affairs;
translations.idiomatic: that envoys negotiating Ili’s return should meet in Ili itself;

sentences.zh: 曰直截議駁，暫聽俄人駐師；

translations.literal: third, direct rejection in negotiation, temporarily allowing Russian troops to remain stationed;
translations.idiomatic: that China reject the treaty outright while temporarily tolerating Russian troops on the ground;

sentences.zh: 曰駐英、法公使不宜遣使俄；

translations.literal: fourth, ministers resident in Britain and France should not be sent as envoys to Russia;
translations.idiomatic: that ministers in London and Paris should not be sent to negotiate with Russia;

sentences.zh: 曰議定崇厚罪名，當稍準萬國公法；

translations.literal: fifth, in fixing Chonghou’s guilt, international law should be followed somewhat;
translations.idiomatic: that Chonghou’s punishment should conform more closely to international law;

sentences.zh: 曰廷臣主戰，止一隅見，當斟酌情理之平。

translations.literal: sixth, court ministers who advocate war see only one corner and should weigh what is fair in reason and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: and that war-minded courtiers saw only one side of the issue and should weigh the balance of justice and expediency.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其見確。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his views as sound.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his judgment.

sentences.zh: 已而召曾紀澤使俄，卒改約。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zeng Jize was summoned as envoy to Russia and ultimately revised the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize was then sent to Russia and eventually secured a revised treaty.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾雖家居，然頗關心君國。

translations.literal: Although Songshen lived in retirement, he still cared greatly for ruler and state.
translations.idiomatic: Though retired, Songshen still followed affairs of state closely.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮亂作，法越釁開，皆有所論列。

translations.literal: When turmoil arose in Korea and the French–Vietnamese conflict opened, he set forth opinions on each.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on the Korean crisis and the opening of the French–Vietnamese war alike.

sentences.zh: 逮馬江敗，恭親王奕訢等去位，言路持政府益亟，嵩燾獨憂之。

translations.literal: When the defeat at Mawei came, Prince Gong Yixin and others left office, and the censorate pressed the government ever more urgently; Songshen alone was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Mawei, Prince Gong and others fell from power while censors hammered the government ever harder; Songshen alone grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「宋以來士夫好名，致誤人家國事。

translations.literal: He once said: "Since the Song, scholar-officials have loved reputation and thereby harmed the affairs of families and states.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote: "Since the Song, literati have chased reputation and ruined the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 託攘外美名，圖不次峻擢；

translations.literal: They borrow the fine name of resisting foreigners to seek extraordinary rapid promotion;
translations.idiomatic: They wrap themselves in the banner of resisting foreigners to win sudden promotion;

sentences.zh: 洎事任屬，變故興，遷就倉皇，周章失措。

translations.literal: but when responsibility falls to them and crises arise, they shift hastily and lose composure in every direction.
translations.idiomatic: yet once responsibility falls on them and crisis strikes, they panic and lose their bearings.

sentences.zh: 生心害政，莫斯為甚！」

translations.literal: To harm government by such motives—nothing exceeds this!"
translations.idiomatic: Nothing harms governance more than such vanity."

sentences.zh: 是疏傳於外，時議咸斥之。

translations.literal: When this memorial circulated abroad, opinion of the time all condemned it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial leaked, contemporaries denounced him roundly.

sentences.zh: 及庚子禍作，其言始大驗，而嵩燾已於十七年卒矣。

translations.literal: When the disaster of Gengzi occurred, his words were greatly vindicated, but Songshen had already died in the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer catastrophe of 1900 his warnings seemed prophetic, but Songshen had died seventeen years earlier.

sentences.zh: 箸有禮記質疑四十九卷，大學中庸質疑三卷，訂正家禮六卷，周易釋例四卷，毛詩約義二卷，綏邊徵實二十四卷，詩文集若干卷。

translations.literal: He authored Doubts on the Record of Rites in forty-nine juan, Doubts on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean in three juan, Revised Family Rituals in six juan, Exemplary Interpretations of the Changes in four juan, Concise Meanings of the Mao Odes in two juan, Verifiable Facts on Pacifying the Frontier in twenty-four juan, and several juan of poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included forty-nine juan of Doubts on the Record of Rites, three juan on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, six juan of Revised Family Rituals, four juan of Exemplary Interpretations of the Changes, two juan of Concise Meanings of the Mao Odes, twenty-four juan of Verifiable Facts on Pacifying the Frontier, and collected literary works.

sentences.zh: 其弟昆燾，字意城。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kunzhen, style name Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kunzhen, courtesy name Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 以舉人參張亮基戎幕，與宗棠俱。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he joined Zhang Liangji’s military staff together with Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served on Zhang Liangji’s staff alongside Zuo Zongtang.

sentences.zh: 李開方擾湖北，自懷慶折而南，武昌夜半得報，亟調師會鵝公頸。

translations.literal: Li Kaifang harassed Hubei, turning south from Huaiqing; Wuchang received word at midnight and urgently moved troops to assemble at Egongjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Kaifang raided Hubei, marching south from Huaiqing, Wuchang got the alarm at midnight and rushed troops to Egongjing.

sentences.zh: 驟遇寇，寇出不意，大擾亂，遂斬開方，殲其軍。

translations.literal: They suddenly met the rebels; the rebels, caught unawares, were greatly thrown into disorder, and Kaifang was beheaded and his army annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: They struck the rebels by surprise, threw them into chaos, beheaded Kaifang, and destroyed his force.

sentences.zh: 報至，亮基始知之，昆燾恆以是自喜。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, Liangji learned of it only then; Kunzhen always took pride in this.
translations.idiomatic: Liangji learned of the victory only when the report arrived; Kunzhen always counted it among his proudest deeds.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章撫湘，昆燾從國藩東征，宗棠援浙，軍資並倚之。

translations.literal: When Luo Bingzhang governed Hunan, Kunzhen followed Guofan on the eastern campaign and Zongtang aided Zhejiang; military funds depended on both.
translations.idiomatic: Under Luo Bingzhang’s governorship of Hunan, Kunzhen marched east with Zeng Guofan while Zuo Zongtang fought in Zhejiang; both campaigns relied on his logistics.

sentences.zh: 由國子監助教歷加四品卿。

translations.literal: From assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy he was promoted step by step to fourth-rank grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Hanlin assistant instructor to fourth-rank court secretary.

sentences.zh: 後劉昆討黔苗，昆燾久引疾歸，力起贊軍事。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Kun campaigned against the Miao of Guizhou, Kunzhen had long retired on grounds of illness but roused himself to assist military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kun campaigned against the Guizhou Miao, Kunzhen had been retired for illness but threw himself back into the war effort.

sentences.zh: 苗將平，又辭去。

translations.literal: When the Miao were nearly pacified, he resigned again.
translations.idiomatic: As the campaign neared its end, he resigned once more.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1882.

sentences.zh: 崇厚，字地山，完顏氏，內務府鑲黃旗人，河督麟慶子。

translations.literal: Chonghou, style name Dishan, of the Wanyan clan, a bannerman of the Imperial Household Department’s Bordered Yellow Banner, son of river commissioner Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou, courtesy name Dishan, of the Wanyan clan, belonged to the Imperial Household’s Bordered Yellow Banner and was the son of river commissioner Lin Qing.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in 1849.

sentences.zh: 選知階州，歷遷長蘆鹽運使。

translations.literal: He was selected as magistrate of Jiezhou and was transferred in succession to Changlu salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jiezhou and later became Changlu salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，署鹽政，疏請停領餘引，代銷滯引，依永平低價。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he acted as salt administrator and memorialized requesting cessation of drawing surplus quotas, substitution for selling stagnant quotas, and pricing according to Yongping’s low rate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, acting as salt administrator, he memorialized to stop issuing surplus salt tickets, clear backlog tickets, and price salt at Yongping’s lower rate.

sentences.zh: 會僧格林沁治畿輔水田，又勸墾葛沽、鹽水沽沃鹵地四千二百餘畝。

translations.literal: When Sengge Rinchen managed paddy fields in the capital region, he also urged reclamation of more than four thousand two hundred mu of fertile saline land at Gegu and Yanshuigu.
translations.idiomatic: While Sengge Rinchen developed paddy in the capital region, Chonghou promoted reclaiming more than 4,200 mu of saline but fertile land at Gegu and Yanshuigu.

sentences.zh: 明年，充三口通商大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he served as commissioner for the three treaty ports.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became commissioner for the three treaty ports.

sentences.zh: 又明年，遷大理寺卿，仍留津與英、法重修租界條約。

translations.literal: The year after that he was transferred to president of the Court of Revision, remaining at Tianjin to revise the concession treaties with Britain and France.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became president of the Court of Revision but stayed in Tianjin to renegotiate the British and French concession treaties.

sentences.zh: 同治改元，以兵部侍郎參直隸軍事，尋署總督。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Tongzhi he served as vice minister of war participating in Zhili military affairs, and soon acted as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongzhi came to the throne he joined Zhili military planning as vice minister of war and soon acted as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 時葡萄牙遣使入京乞換約，崇厚牒請總署摽勿受。

translations.literal: At that time Portugal sent an envoy to the capital requesting treaty revision; Chonghou memorialized the Zongli Yamen to mark and refuse reception.
translations.idiomatic: When Portugal sent an envoy to Beijing to revise its treaty, Chonghou urged the Zongli Yamen to refuse him.

sentences.zh: 法使哥士耆緩頰，治蒞津，朝命崇厚承其事。

translations.literal: The French minister Gros mediated, came to govern at Tianjin, and the court ordered Chonghou to undertake the matter.
translations.idiomatic: French minister Gros interceded and took charge at Tianjin; the court put Chonghou in charge of the negotiations.

sentences.zh: 次年，諭遏冀州竄匪，坐失機，被責。

translations.literal: The next year he was ordered to check bandits fleeing in Jizhou; for missing the opportunity he was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was ordered to stop bandits raiding Jizhou; blamed for missing his chance, he was censured.

sentences.zh: 已而丹使踵葡例，拒如初。

translations.literal: Soon the Danish envoy followed the Portuguese precedent and was refused as before.
translations.idiomatic: When a Danish envoy followed the Portuguese example, Chonghou refused him as well.

sentences.zh: 復命為全權大臣，訂約五十五條，通商章程九款。

translations.literal: He was again appointed plenipotentiary minister and concluded a treaty of fifty-five articles and nine articles of commercial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named plenipotentiary and signed a fifty-five-article treaty with nine commercial clauses.

sentences.zh: 自是而荷、而日、而比、而意、而奧，皆遣使求取，並為延款，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: From this the Dutch, Japanese, Belgians, Italians, and Austrians all sent envoys seeking treaties, and he entertained them all; details are in the record of foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Dutch, Japanese, Belgians, Italians, and Austrians all sent envoys seeking treaties, which he received in turn; the full account appears in the foreign-relations annals.

sentences.zh: 復建議設北洋機器局城南分局，城堞砲台與郡城遙相峙。

translations.literal: He again proposed establishing a southern branch of the Beiyang Machine Works, with ramparts and batteries standing opposite the prefectural city at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed a southern branch of the Beiyang Arsenal, with ramparts and batteries facing the prefectural seat across the river.

sentences.zh: 五年，貸款墾海河北岸，首邢家沽訖臥河村，中洩為渠，闢稻田可五百頃，手訂試墾章程，於是兩岸為沃野。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he borrowed funds to reclaim the north bank of the Hai River from Xingjiagu to Wohe Village; a channel was cut through the middle and paddy fields of about five hundred qing were opened; he personally drafted trial-reclamation regulations, and thus both banks became fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he borrowed money to reclaim the north bank of the Hai from Xingjiagu to Wohe Village, cut an irrigation channel, and opened some five hundred qing of paddy; he drafted the trial-reclamation rules himself, turning both banks into rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 九年，津郡民、教失和，被議。

translations.literal: In the ninth year discord arose between people and missionaries in Tianjin prefecture, and he was criticized.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, after the Tianjin church conflict, he came under censure.

sentences.zh: 事寧，朝廷遣使修好，命充出使法國大臣，是為專使一國之始，然事畢即返。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled the court sent an envoy to restore relations and appointed him minister to France; this was the beginning of envoys dedicated to a single country, yet he returned as soon as the business was done.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, the court sent him as envoy to France—the first minister assigned to a single country—but he returned as soon as his mission ended.

sentences.zh: 歷署戶部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting vice minister of revenue and of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted as vice minister of revenue and of personnel.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，署奉天將軍，疏請擇地設官，置寬甸、懷仁、通化三縣，增邊關兵備道，昇昌圖為府，改八家鎮為縣，徙經歷駐康家屯，改梨樹城為廳，徙照磨駐八面城；

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he acted as general of Fengtian and memorialized requesting selection of sites to establish officials, creating the three counties of Kuandian, Huairen, and Tonghua, adding a frontier defense circuit, promoting Changtu to a prefecture, changing Bajiazhen to a county and moving the assistant magistrate to Kangjiatun, changing Lishucheng to a subprefecture and moving the registrar to Bamiancheng;
translations.idiomatic: In 1876, as acting general of Fengtian, he memorialized to establish local government in newly opened territory: three counties at Kuandian, Huairen, and Tonghua; a frontier defense circuit; Changtu raised to prefecture; Bajiazhen made a county with the assistant magistrate at Kangjiatun; Lishucheng made a subprefecture with the registrar at Bamiancheng;

sentences.zh: 其通判、知縣並加理事同知銜，兼治蒙民，議行。

translations.literal: their subprefects and magistrates were all given the additional title of subprefect administering Mongol affairs, concurrently governing Mongol subjects, and the plan was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: subprefects and magistrates were given concurrent titles as Mongol affairs administrators, and the plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 先後疏論吉林積弊，請辦馬賊，懲聚博，清積訟，覈荒地，除金匪。

translations.literal: In succession he memorialized on chronic abuses in Jilin, requesting suppression of horse bandits, punishment of gambling gatherings, clearing of accumulated lawsuits, verification of wasteland, and elimination of gold bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized repeatedly on Jilin’s chronic problems, urging action against horse bandits, gambling rings, backlog of lawsuits, unregistered wasteland, and gold thieves.

sentences.zh: 又以私墾圍場者眾，為懇寬其既往，已墾者量丈昇科，未墾者擇地安插，仍留隙地以講武，稱旨。

translations.literal: Because many had privately reclaimed imperial hunting grounds, he pleaded to pardon past offenses: for those already reclaimed, measure and register for taxation; for those not yet reclaimed, choose sites for resettlement, while still leaving gaps for military drill—the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Many had illegally farmed imperial hunting grounds; he asked clemency for past offenses, taxation for land already cleared, resettlement elsewhere for the rest, and open space left for military drill. The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，俄界回寇擾邊，與其外部格爾斯合力禁止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Hui bandits on the Russian border harassed the frontier; together with the Russian foreign ministry Giers he jointly suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Hui raiders on the Russian border troubled the frontier; he worked with Russian foreign minister Giers to stop them.

sentences.zh: 其秋，授出使俄國大臣，加內大臣銜，晉左都御史。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed minister to Russia, with the additional title of grand minister of the interior, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was named envoy to Russia, given the rank of grand minister of the interior, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年，赴俄。

translations.literal: The next year he went to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he traveled to Russia.

sentences.zh: 初，左宗棠進兵伊犁，乘俄土戰爭，要俄人退去庫爾札，俄人多所挾求。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zuo Zongtang advanced on Ili, taking advantage of the Russo-Turkish War to demand that the Russians withdraw from Kulja; the Russians made many demands in return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zuo Zongtang marched on Ili during the Russo-Turkish War, he pressed Russia to evacuate Kulja, but the Russians drove a hard bargain.

sentences.zh: 至是，崇厚抵利伐第亞謁俄皇達使命，貿然與訂和約：一，自嘉峪關迳西安、漢中達漢口，俄有通商權；

translations.literal: At this point Chonghou reached Livadia, paid homage to the Russian emperor to fulfill his mission, and rashly concluded a peace treaty: first, from Jiayuguan through Xi'an and Hanzhong to Hankou, Russia would have trading rights;
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou then reached Livadia, presented his credentials to the tsar, and rashly signed a treaty granting Russia trading rights from Jiayuguan through Xi'an and Hanzhong to Hankou;

sentences.zh: 一，自松花江至伯都訥，貿易自由；

translations.literal: second, from the Songhua River to Boduna, trade would be free;
translations.idiomatic: free trade along the Songhua from its mouth to Boduna;

sentences.zh: 一，自蒙古及天山南北輸入商品，不課稅金；

translations.literal: third, goods imported from Mongolia and north and south of the Tianshan would pay no tax;
translations.idiomatic: duty-free import of goods from Mongolia and both sides of the Tianshan;

sentences.zh: 一，自西伯利亞至張家口，歸俄敷設鐵道；

translations.literal: fourth, from Siberia to Zhangjiakou, Russia would lay railways;
translations.idiomatic: Russian rights to build railways from Siberia to Zhangjiakou;

sentences.zh: 一，自陝甘至漢口，既榷常稅，其雜稅概免；

translations.literal: fifth, from Shaanxi-Gansu to Hankou, after the regular transit levy, miscellaneous taxes would all be exempt;
translations.idiomatic: after paying the regular transit tax from Shaanxi-Gansu to Hankou, exemption from all miscellaneous levies;

sentences.zh: 一，嘉峪關、科布多、哈密、吐魯番、烏魯木齊、庫車置領事官；

translations.literal: sixth, consuls would be stationed at Jiayuguan, Kobdo, Hami, Turfan, Urumqi, and Kucha;
translations.idiomatic: consuls at Jiayuguan, Kobdo, Hami, Turfan, Urumqi, and Kucha;

sentences.zh: 一，凡俄國臣民旅華，許攜銃器；

translations.literal: seventh, all Russian subjects traveling in China would be permitted to carry firearms;
translations.idiomatic: permission for Russian subjects in China to carry firearms;

sentences.zh: 一，伊犁城及旁近地，凡俄所有土地及建築物，不在還付例。

translations.literal: eighth, in Ili city and nearby areas, all Russian-owned land and buildings would not fall under the rule of restitution.
translations.idiomatic: and retention by Russia of all land and buildings in and around Ili city, exempt from return to China.

sentences.zh: 約成，朝野譁然，於是修撰王仁堪、洗馬張之洞等交章論劾。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded, court and populace were in an uproar; thereupon compiler Wang Renkan, palace aide Zhang Zhidong, and others submitted memorials in succession impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: When the treaty became public, outrage swept court and country. Compiler Wang Renkan, palace aide Zhang Zhidong, and others filed impeachment memorials one after another.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，下崇厚獄，定斬監候，以徇俄人請，貸死，仍羈禁。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, imprisoned Chonghou, sentenced him to decapitation with imprisonment pending, and to satisfy the Russian request commuted the death sentence but still kept him in custody.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, threw Chonghou in prison, and sentenced him to death with reprieve. To satisfy Russia he spared his life but kept him confined.

sentences.zh: 更遣曾紀澤往俄更約，爭回伊犁南路七百餘裡，嘉峪關諸地緩置官。

translations.literal: Zeng Jize was further sent to Russia to revise the treaty, recovering more than seven hundred li of the southern Ili road and deferring consular placement at Jiayuguan and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize was then sent to renegotiate, recovering over seven hundred li of southern Ili and postponing consular posts at Jiayuguan and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 十年，崇厚輸銀三十萬濟軍，釋歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Chonghou contributed three hundred thousand taels of silver to support the army and was released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he donated 300,000 taels for the army and was released.

sentences.zh: 遇太后五旬萬壽，隨班祝嘏，朝旨依原官降二級，賞給職銜。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager’s fiftieth birthday celebration came, he joined the court in offering congratulations; an edict reduced him two ranks from his original office and granted a nominal title.
translations.idiomatic: At the empress dowager’s fiftieth birthday he joined the court congratulations; the throne reduced him two ranks from his former office but granted a nominal title.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 曾紀澤，字劼剛，大學士國藩子。

translations.literal: Zeng Jize, style name Jiegang, was the son of Grand Secretary Guofan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize, courtesy name Jiegang, was the son of Grand Secretary Zeng Guofan.

sentences.zh: 少負俊才。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed exceptional talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 以廕補戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of Revenue by hereditary privilege as vice director.

sentences.zh: 父憂服除，襲侯爵。

translations.literal: When mourning for his father ended, he inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: After his father’s mourning period he inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，充出使英法大臣，補太常寺少卿，轉大理寺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he served as minister to Britain and France, was appointed vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he became envoy to Britain and France, then vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 六年，使俄大臣崇厚獲罪去，以紀澤兼之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the minister to Russia Chonghou was dismissed for guilt, and Jize was given the post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880, when Chonghou fell from office, Jize was given the Russian mission as well.

sentences.zh: 先是俄乘我內亂，據伊犁，及回部平，乃舉以還我，議定界、通商。

translations.literal: Earlier Russia had seized Ili during our internal turmoil; when the Muslim regions were pacified it was to be returned to us, and boundaries and trade were to be negotiated.
translations.idiomatic: Russia had seized Ili during China’s civil wars; after the Muslim regions were pacified, Moscow agreed to return it and negotiate borders and trade.

sentences.zh: 崇厚不請旨，遽署押，所定約多失權利，因詔紀澤兼使俄，議改前約。

translations.literal: Chonghou did not request instructions but hastily signed and sealed; the treaty he fixed lost many rights, and therefore Jize was ordered to serve concurrently as envoy to Russia to negotiate revision of the prior treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou signed without imperial authorization, conceding far too much. The court ordered Jize to revise the treaty.

sentences.zh: 俄以崇厚罹大辟，怫甚。

translations.literal: Russia, because Chonghou faced capital punishment, was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Russia was furious that Chonghou faced execution.

sentences.zh: 紀澤慮礙交涉，請貸崇厚死，上許之，論監禁。

translations.literal: Jize feared this would obstruct negotiations and requested sparing Chonghou’s life; the emperor approved and ordered imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Jize feared this would block negotiations and asked the emperor to spare Chonghou’s life; the court commuted the sentence to imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 紀澤乃疏言：「伊犁一役，辦法有三：曰戰，守，和。

translations.literal: Jize then memorialized: "For the Ili affair there are three methods: called war, defense, and peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jize then wrote: "On Ili there are three approaches: war, holding back, and negotiation.

sentences.zh: 言戰者，謂左宗棠等席全勝之勢，不難一戰。

translations.literal: Those who speak of war say that Zuo Zongtang and others, enjoying the momentum of complete victory, would not find one battle difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Advocates of war argued that Zuo Zongtang, riding a string of victories, could easily fight again.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂伊犁地形岩險，俄為強敵，非西陲比。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to say that Ili’s terrain is precipitous and dangerous, Russia is a powerful enemy, and it is not comparable to the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Ili’s terrain is forbidding and Russia a far stronger foe than the rebels of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 兵戎一啟，後患滋長。

translations.literal: Once arms are raised, later troubles multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Once war begins, the troubles will only multiply.

sentences.zh: 東三省與俄毗連，根本重地，防不勝防。

translations.literal: The three eastern provinces border Russia; they are fundamental vital territory, impossible to defend fully.
translations.idiomatic: The three eastern provinces border Russia—China’s heartland—and cannot be fully defended.

sentences.zh: 或欲遊說歐邦，使相牽制，是特戰國之陳言耳。

translations.literal: Some wish to lobby European states to restrain one another; this is merely the stale talk of the Warring States period.
translations.idiomatic: Some propose enlisting European powers to check Russia—a Warring States stratagem, not a serious policy.

sentences.zh: 各邦雖外和內忌，而協以謀我則同，孰肯出而相助？

translations.literal: Though the various states are outwardly harmonious and inwardly jealous, in plotting against us they are the same—who would come forth to help?
translations.idiomatic: European powers may quarrel among themselves, but they unite against China. Who would help us?

sentences.zh: 言守者，則謂伊犁邊境，若多糜巨帑以獲之，是鶩荒遠、潰腹心也，不如棄而勿收。

translations.literal: Those who speak of defense say that on the Ili border, if great funds are squandered to obtain it, this is contending for the remote and barren while draining the heartland—better to abandon and not recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders of inaction say that pouring treasure into distant Ili drains the heartland for barren borderland better left alone.

sentences.zh: 不知開國以來，經營西域者至矣。

translations.literal: They do not know that since the founding of the dynasty, management of the Western Regions has been utmost.
translations.idiomatic: They forget how much every dynasty since the founding has invested in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 聖祖、世宗不憚勤天下力以征討之，至乾隆二十二年，伊犁底定，腹地始得安枕。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor and Shizong did not shrink from mobilizing the strength of the empire to campaign; by the twenty-second year of Qianlong Ili was settled, and only then could the interior sleep in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi and Yongzheng mobilized the empire to conquer the west; by 1757 Ili was pacified and the interior could rest secure.

sentences.zh: 今若棄之，如新疆何？

translations.literal: If we abandon it now, what of Xinjiang?
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon Ili now, what becomes of Xinjiang?

sentences.zh: 說者謂姑紓吾力以俟後圖。

translations.literal: Advocates say for the moment ease our strength and wait for later plans.
translations.idiomatic: Some say we should husband our strength for a later day.

sentences.zh: 不知左宗棠等軍，將召之使還乎？

translations.literal: They do not know whether Zuo Zongtang’s army and the like will be summoned to return?
translations.idiomatic: Will we recall Zuo Zongtang’s armies?

sentences.zh: 則經界未明，緩急何以應變？

translations.literal: Then boundaries are unclear—how respond to urgency and ease?
translations.idiomatic: If borders remain unsettled, how can we respond when crisis strikes?

sentences.zh: 抑任其逍遙境上，則難於轉餉，銳氣坐銷。

translations.literal: Or if they are left to roam the borderlands, it is hard to transport supplies and keen spirit is wasted in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave them idle on the frontier, supply lines fail and fighting spirit fades.

sentences.zh: 是今日之事，戰、守皆不足恃，仍不外言和。

translations.literal: Thus in today’s affair, war and defense are both insufficient to rely on; still nothing lies outside speaking of peace.
translations.idiomatic: War and passivity alike are unreliable; negotiation remains the only path.

sentences.zh: 和亦有辦法三：曰分界，通商，償款其小者也。

translations.literal: Peace also has three methods: called boundary demarcation, trade, and indemnity—these are the lesser matters.
translations.idiomatic: Negotiation too has three elements: borders, trade, and indemnity—the last being least important.

sentences.zh: 即通商亦較分界為輕。

translations.literal: Even trade is lighter than boundary demarcation.
translations.idiomatic: Even trade matters less than borders.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 西國定約之例，有常守不渝者，亦有隨時修改者。

translations.literal: In Western nations’ practice of fixing treaties, some are permanently observed without change and some may be revised from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Western treaty practice distinguishes provisions that are permanent from those subject to periodic revision.

sentences.zh: 不渝者，分界是也。

translations.literal: What is not changed is boundary demarcation.
translations.idiomatic: Borders are permanent.

sentences.zh: 此益則彼損。

translations.literal: Where this side gains, that side loses.
translations.idiomatic: One side’s gain is the other’s loss.

sentences.zh: 是以定約之時，其難其慎。

translations.literal: Therefore at the time of fixing a treaty, the difficulty and caution are extreme.
translations.idiomatic: That is why border treaties demand the greatest care.

sentences.zh: 修改者，通商是也。

translations.literal: What may be revised is trade.
translations.idiomatic: Trade clauses may be revised.

sentences.zh: 若干年修改一次。

translations.literal: Every certain number of years they are revised once.
translations.idiomatic: They are renegotiated every few years.

sentences.zh: 條文之不善，商務之受損，正賴此修改之年可​​以換約，固非彼族所得專也。

translations.literal: Poor clauses and harm to commerce precisely rely on these years of revision to exchange treaties; it is certainly not something the other race alone may monopolize.
translations.idiomatic: Faulty clauses and commercial losses can be corrected at revision—an opportunity not reserved for foreigners alone.

sentences.zh: 俄約經崇厚議定，俄君署押，今欲全數更換，勢所不能。

translations.literal: The Russian treaty was negotiated by Chonghou and signed by the Russian sovereign; now to wish to replace it entirely is impossible in the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou’s treaty was signed by the tsar; we cannot expect to replace it wholesale.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為分界既屬常守之局，必當堅持力爭。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly believes that since boundary demarcation belongs to the permanently observed pattern, one must firmly insist and strive.
translations.idiomatic: I believe we must fight hardest on borders, which are permanent.

sentences.zh: 若通商各條，惟當去其太甚，其餘從權應允，俟諸異日之修改，庶和局可終保全。

translations.literal: As for the various trade articles, one should only remove what is excessive; the rest may be granted as expedient, awaiting revision on another day—then perhaps the peace settlement can ultimately be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: On trade, we should reject only the worst excesses and concede the rest, reserving revision for later, so the peace may hold.

sentences.zh: 不然，事機決裂，必須聲罪致討，此戰之說也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, when affairs rupture, one must proclaim guilt and launch punitive action—this is the argument for war.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the rupture will force us to declare war and fight—back to the war party’s position.

sentences.zh: 廟堂勝算，固非使臣所敢議也。

translations.literal: The court’s strategic calculations are certainly not what an envoy dares discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Grand strategy is not for an envoy to debate.

sentences.zh: 不然，暫置伊犁勿論，此守之說也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, temporarily set Ili aside without discussion—this is the argument for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Or we could set Ili aside for now—the passive party’s view.

sentences.zh: 是邊界不可稍讓，而全境轉可盡捐，臣亦未敢以為是也。

translations.literal: This is that the border cannot be yielded slightly, yet the whole territory may be entirely abandoned—I also dare not consider this correct.
translations.idiomatic: That would mean refusing any border concession while surrendering the whole region—I cannot accept that either.

sentences.zh: 再不然，姑先為駁議，俟不得已時酌量允之，此和之說也。

translations.literal: Again otherwise, for the moment first raise objections and wait until unavoidable to grant as appropriate—this is the argument for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Or we could object first and concede only under pressure—a bargaining tactic, not statesmanship.

sentences.zh: 是乃市井售物嘗試之術，非所以敦信義、馭遠人也。

translations.literal: This is merely the trick of market vendors testing prices, not the means to uphold good faith and control distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: That is haggling in the marketplace, not the way to uphold trust and manage foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 蓋準駁貴有一定之計，勿致後日迫於事勢，復有後允之條。

translations.literal: For in fixing what to reject and what to grant, there must be a settled plan, lest later, pressed by circumstances, there again be clauses granted afterward.
translations.idiomatic: We must decide in advance what to reject and what to grant, lest pressure later force further concessions.

sentences.zh: 今臣至俄都，但言兩國和好，自應遣使通誠。

translations.literal: Now that your servant has reached the Russian capital, he will speak only of amity between the two states and that envoys should naturally be sent to communicate sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: In St. Petersburg I shall speak only of friendship between our nations and the need for diplomatic communication.

sentences.zh: 至辨論公事，傳達語言，系使臣職分，俟接奉本國文牘，再行商議。

translations.literal: As for debating public business and conveying language, these fall within the envoy’s duty; he will wait until receiving documents from his own state before negotiating further.
translations.idiomatic: Official negotiations and formal statements are my duty; I shall wait for instructions from Beijing before discussing terms.

sentences.zh: 如此立言，庶不至見拒鄰邦，貽國羞辱。

translations.literal: Speaking thus, perhaps he will not be rejected by the neighboring state or bring shame on the nation.
translations.idiomatic: This approach may keep Russia from rejecting us and spare the nation humiliation.

sentences.zh: 臣駑下，唯有懍遵聖訓，不激不隨，冀收得尺得寸之功，稍維大局。」

translations.literal: Your servant is dull and lowly; he can only reverently follow the sacred instruction, neither provoking nor yielding, hoping to gain inch by inch some achievement and slightly preserve the great situation."
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy, but I shall follow Your Majesty’s instruction—neither provocative nor submissive—in hopes of gaining inch by inch and preserving the larger peace."

sentences.zh: 及至俄，日與俄外部及駐華公使布策等反复辨論，凡數十萬言，十閱月而議始定。

translations.literal: When he reached Russia, day by day with the Russian foreign ministry and the minister to China Busty and others he debated back and forth, altogether several hundred thousand words; after ten months the negotiations were settled.
translations.idiomatic: In Russia he debated daily with Foreign Minister Giers, minister Busty, and others—hundreds of thousands of words over ten months before terms were fixed.

sentences.zh: 崇厚原約，僅得伊犁之半，岩險屬俄如故。

translations.literal: Under Chonghou’s original treaty China obtained only half of Ili; precipitous strong points still belonged to Russia as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou’s treaty had left China only half of Ili, with the strategic heights still in Russian hands.

sentences.zh: 紀澤爭回南境之烏宗島山、帖克斯川要隘，然後伊犁拱宸諸城足以自守，且得與喀什噶爾、阿克蘇諸城通行無阻。

translations.literal: Jize recovered the southern passes of Wuzongdao Mountain and the Tekes River, so that then the cities of Ili, Gongchen, and others could defend themselves and communication with Kashgar, Aksu, and other cities would be unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jize won back the southern passes at Wuzongdao and the Tekes River, so Ili and Gongchen could be defended and routes to Kashgar and Aksu kept open.

sentences.zh: 其他分界及通商條文，亦多所釐正焉。

translations.literal: Other boundary and trade articles were also extensively corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Many other border and trade clauses were corrected as well.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷宗人府府丞、左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he became vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，留任三載。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he remained in office three more years.
translations.idiomatic: His term was extended for three years.

sentences.zh: 法越構釁，紀澤與法抗辯不稍屈，疏陳備禦六策。

translations.literal: When France and Vietnam provoked conflict, Jize argued against France without yielding slightly and memorialized six policies for defense preparations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-French crisis he held firm in debate with France and submitted six defense proposals.

sentences.zh: 十年，晉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 與英人議定洋藥稅釐，歲增銀六百餘萬。

translations.literal: With the English he negotiated opium tax and transit levies, increasing revenue by more than six million taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: He negotiated opium duties with Britain, adding more than six million taels a year to revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，還朝，轉入總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to court and transferred into the Zongli Yamen for all nations’ affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned home and joined the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 調戶部，兼署刑部、吏部各侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently acted as vice minister of justice and of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently acted as vice minister of justice and personnel.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒，加太子少保，諡惠敏。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died; he was given the posthumous title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the temple name Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1890, posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the temple name Huimin.

sentences.zh: 子廣鑾，左副都御史；

translations.literal: His son Guangluan, left vice censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangluan became left vice censor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 廣銓，兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: Guangquan, vice director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Guangquan, vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 薛福成，字叔耘，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Xue Fucheng, style name Shuyun, was a native of Wuxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fucheng, courtesy name Shuyun, came from Wuxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 以副貢生參曾國藩戎幕，積勞至直隸州知州。

translations.literal: As a tribute student of the second rank he joined Zeng Guofan’s military staff; through accumulated service he rose to prefect of Zhili prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a tribute student he joined Zeng Guofan’s staff and rose through service to prefect of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒初元，下詔求言，福成上治平六策，又密議海防十事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu an edict sought opinions; Fucheng submitted six policies for good governance and also privately discussed ten matters of coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxu sought policy advice in 1875, Fucheng submitted six governance proposals and ten confidential coastal-defense recommendations.

sentences.zh: 時總稅務司赫德喜言事，總署議授為總海防司，福成上書力爭，乃止。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector General of Customs Hart liked to speak on affairs; the Zongli Yamen debated appointing him director-general of coastal defense; Fucheng memorialized in strenuous opposition and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Customs chief Hart had proposed taking charge of coastal defense; Fucheng protested vigorously and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝鮮亂，張樹聲代李鴻章督畿輔，聞變，將牒總署奏請發兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year turmoil arose in Korea; Zhang Shusheng replaced Li Hongzhang as governor-general of the capital region; hearing of the crisis, he was about to memorialize the Zongli Yamen requesting troop dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882, when Korea erupted in violence, Zhang Shusheng, who had replaced Li Hongzhang in Zhili, prepared to ask the Zongli Yamen for troops.

sentences.zh: 福成慮緩則蹈琉球覆轍，請速發軍艦東渡援之。

translations.literal: Fucheng feared that delay would repeat the Ryukyu precedent and requested rapid dispatch of warships east across the sea to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a repeat of the Ryukyu disaster, he urged immediate dispatch of warships to Korea.

sentences.zh: 亂定，以功遷道員。

translations.literal: When the turmoil was settled, for his merit he was transferred to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十年，授寧紹台道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed intendant of Ningbo, Shaoxing, and Taizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he was appointed intendant of the Ning-Shao-Tai circuit.

sentences.zh: 法蘭西敗盟，構兵越南，詔緣海戒嚴。

translations.literal: France broke the alliance and made war in Vietnam; an edict ordered coastal alert along the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When France broke faith and attacked Vietnam, the coast was placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 寧波故浙東要衢也，方是時，提督歐陽利見頓金雞山，楊岐珍頓招寶山，總兵錢玉興分守要隘。

translations.literal: Ningbo was formerly a vital pass of eastern Zhejiang; at this time Provincial Commander Ouyang Lijian encamped at Jinji Hill, Yang Qizhen at Zhaobao Hill, and Regional Commander Qian Yuxing divided defense of key passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ningbo was Zhejiang’s strategic gateway. Provincial commander Ouyang Lijian held Jinji Hill, Yang Qizhen held Zhaobao Hill, and regional commander Qian Yuxing guarded other passes.

sentences.zh: 諸將故等夷，不相統攝。

translations.literal: The generals were formerly equals and did not command one another.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were equals who did not coordinate with one another.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉秉璋檄福成綜營務，調護諸將，築長牆，釘叢樁，造電線，清間諜，絕鄉導與窺伺。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Bingzhang ordered Fucheng to oversee camp affairs, harmonize the generals, build long walls, drive clustered piles, lay telegraph lines, clear spies, and cut off local guides and scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Bingzhang put Fucheng in charge of defenses: coordinating the generals, building walls, driving pilings, laying telegraph lines, rooting out spies, and blocking guides and scouts.

sentences.zh: 其南洋援台三艦為法人追襲，駛入鎮海口，復令其合力守禦。

translations.literal: Three ships of the southern fleet aiding Taiwan were pursued and attacked by the French and entered Zhenhai harbor; he again ordered them to combine in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Three southern-fleet ships bound for Taiwan, pursued by the French, took refuge in Zhenhai; he ordered them to join the defense.

sentences.zh: 謀甫定而寇氛逼矣，再至，再卻之，卒不得逞而去。

translations.literal: Plans had just been settled when the enemy’s presence pressed close; they came twice and were repelled twice, and in the end could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were barely set when the enemy appeared twice and was twice driven off, finally withdrawing without success.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除湖南按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Hunan provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he was appointed Hunan provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 明年，改三品京堂，出使英法義比四國大臣，歷光祿、太常、大理寺卿，留使如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to third-rank capital official, minister to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium; he passed through president of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Sacrifices, and Revision, remaining envoy as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became a third-rank capital official and envoy to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium, passing through presidencies of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Sacrifices, and Revision while keeping his mission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坎巨提來乞師。

translations.literal: Before long Hunza came to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hunza appealed for military aid.

sentences.zh: 坎故羈縻回部，自英滅克什米爾，遂為所屬。

translations.literal: Hunza was formerly a subordinate of the Muslim regions; since Britain extinguished Kashmir, it came under British control.
translations.idiomatic: Hunza had long been a tributary of the Muslim west; after Britain annexed Kashmir it fell under British sway.

sentences.zh: 近且築路貫其境，坎拒之，戰弗勝，乃求援，朝旨使福成詰其故。

translations.literal: Recently Britain also built a road through its territory; Hunza resisted, was defeated in battle, and then sought aid; a court edict ordered Fucheng to investigate the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Britain then built a road through Hunza; when Hunza resisted and lost, it appealed to China, and the court ordered Fucheng to investigate.

sentences.zh: 福成晤英外部沙力斯伯里，诇知其防俄心切，遂與訂定會立坎酋，以釋嫌怨。

translations.literal: Fucheng met with Salisbury of the British Foreign Office, probed and learned that his desire to guard against Russia was keen, and thereupon jointly arranged to install the Hunza chief together, to dispel suspicion and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fucheng met Lord Salisbury at the Foreign Office, sensed how urgently Britain wished to counter Russia, and agreed with him to recognize a Hunza ruler jointly—an arrangement meant to clear away mutual distrust.

sentences.zh: 因具選立本末以上，並陳英、俄互爭帕米爾狀，請趣俄分界，冀英隱助。

translations.literal: He thereupon prepared a full account of how the chief was chosen and submitted it upward, also setting forth the state of British-Russian contention over the Pamirs, requesting that Russia be pressed to delimit the border, hoping Britain would secretly assist.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court with a full report on the selection of the chief, described Anglo-Russian rivalry in the Pamirs, and urged Moscow to settle the boundary—counting on quiet British backing.

sentences.zh: 已而被命集議滇緬界線、商務。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to convene deliberations on the Yunnan-Burma boundary line and commercial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon instructed to take part in negotiations over the Yunnan–Burma frontier and trade.

sentences.zh: 先是曾紀澤使英，謀將南掌、拈人諸土司盡為我屬，議未決而歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zeng Jize was envoy to Britain, he had sought to bring all the chieftaincies of Lan Xang and the Nai people under Chinese authority; the matter was unresolved when he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Jize had served in London he tried to place the Lan Xang and Nai chieftaincies entirely under Qing rule, but left before the plan was settled.

sentences.zh: 至是福成繼之，始變前規，稍拓邊界，訂定條約二十款，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: When Fucheng succeeded him, he first altered the previous policy, slightly expanded the boundary, and finalized a treaty of twenty articles—the details are given in the Treatises on Foreign Relations.
translations.idiomatic: Fucheng took up the post, broke with earlier practice, modestly extended the border, and signed a twenty-article treaty whose particulars appear in the Treatises on Foreign Relations.

sentences.zh: 福成任使事數年，恆惓惓於保商，疏請除舊禁，廣招徠。

translations.literal: During his several years as envoy, Fucheng was constantly devoted to protecting merchants, memorializing to abolish old prohibitions and broadly recruit trade.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his years abroad he kept merchant protection foremost, urging the court to lift outdated bans and invite more trade.

sentences.zh: 其爭設南洋各島領事官，尤持正義，英人終亦從之。

translations.literal: His insistence on establishing consular officials on the various islands of the Nanyang was especially principled; the British finally acceded.
translations.idiomatic: He fought especially hard—and on principled grounds—for consuls across the South Seas islands, and London eventually agreed.

sentences.zh: 又以英、法教案牽涉既廣，條列治本治標機宜甚悉。

translations.literal: Because the British and French missionary cases had grown so widespread in their ramifications, he also itemized measures for addressing root causes and symptoms with great thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: As Sino-British and Sino-French missionary disputes had spread ever wider, he laid out detailed remedies both immediate and structural.

sentences.zh: 其將歸也，复撮舉見聞上疏以陳，大恉謂宜厲人才，整戎備，濬利源，重使職，為棄短集長之策。

translations.literal: When he was about to return, he again summarized what he had observed and submitted a memorial, its main import being that talent should be cultivated, military readiness strengthened, sources of profit dredged open, and the duties of envoys weighted heavily—a policy of discarding weaknesses and gathering strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving post he submitted a sweeping memorial drawn from his observations, arguing that China should develop talent, rebuild defenses, unlock economic gain, and restore dignity to diplomacy—a strategy of turning weaknesses into strengths.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，歸，至上海病卒，優詔賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he returned and died of illness at Shanghai; an edict of favor granted posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1896 he came home, fell ill at Shanghai, and died; the throne issued a generous posthumous decree.

sentences.zh: 卒後半載，而中英訂附款，致將福成收回各地割棄泰半，論者惜之。

translations.literal: Half a year after his death, China and Britain signed supplementary articles that caused most of the territories Fucheng had recovered to be ceded again; commentators regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Six months later a supplementary Sino-British agreement clawed back most of what he had won, to the regret of many observers.

sentences.zh: 福成好為古文辭，演迆平易，曲盡事理，尤長於論事紀載。

translations.literal: Fucheng loved to compose classical prose; his style unfolded in easy clarity and exhaustively covered matters and principles, especially excelling in discursive essays and historical records.
translations.idiomatic: He was a gifted essayist in the classical vein—plain yet thorough, with a particular gift for argument and narrative.

sentences.zh: 著有庸菴文編、筆記，海外文編，出使英法義比日記，浙東籌防錄。

translations.literal: He authored the Yong'an Collected Prose and Notes, Overseas Collected Prose, Diaries of a Mission to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium, and Records of Coastal Defense Planning in Eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Yong'an wenji and biji, Overseas wenji, Diaries of a Mission to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium, and Records of Eastern Zhejiang Coastal Defense.

sentences.zh: 黎庶昌，字蓴齋，貴州遵義人。

translations.literal: Li Shuchang, style name Chunzhai, was a native of Zunyi in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuchang, courtesy name Chunzhai, came from Zunyi in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 少嗜讀，從鄭珍遊，講求經世學。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading; he studied under Zheng Zhen and pursued practical statecraft learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read voraciously, studied with Zheng Zhen, and devoted himself to statecraft.

sentences.zh: 同治初元，星變，應詔上書論時政，條舉利病甚悉，上嘉之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, when a celestial anomaly appeared, he answered the imperial call to submit a memorial on current affairs, listing benefits and harms with great thoroughness; the throne praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared early in Tongzhi, he responded to the imperial call with a detailed critique of policy; the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 以廩貢生授知縣，交曾國藩差序。

translations.literal: As a stipend-supported senior licentiate he was appointed county magistrate and placed under Zeng Guofan's assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from the ranks of stipend licentiates to county magistrate, he was assigned to Zeng Guofan's staff.

sentences.zh: 國藩素重鄭氏，接庶昌延入幕，歷署吳江、青浦諸邑；

translations.literal: Guofan had always held the Zheng family in esteem; he received Shuchang and invited him into his staff, and he served in acting posts in Wujiang, Qingpu, and other districts;
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, who respected the Zheng school, took Shuchang into his secretariat; Shuchang later acted as magistrate in Wujiang, Qingpu, and elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 兩筦榷關，稅驟進。

translations.literal: Twice he managed customs stations, and tax receipts surged.
translations.idiomatic: and twice ran customs posts, each time sharply increasing revenue.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，郭嵩燾出使英國，調充參贊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, when Guo Songshen went as envoy to Britain, Shuchang was transferred to serve as counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876, when Guo Songshen went to London, Shuchang joined the mission as counselor.

sentences.zh: 歷比、瑞、葡、奧諸邦，箸書以撮所聞見，成西洋雜誌。

translations.literal: He traveled through Belgium, Sweden, Portugal, Austria, and other states, and wrote a book gathering what he had heard and seen, producing Miscellaneous Notes on the West.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Belgium, Sweden, Portugal, Austria, and beyond, he compiled his observations into Miscellaneous Notes on the West.

sentences.zh: 晉道員。

translations.literal: He was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，命充出使日本大臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed minister to Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was named minister to Japan.

sentences.zh: 值議琉球案及華商雜居事，其外部井上馨持甚堅，庶昌翻复辨論，卒如所議。

translations.literal: When the Ryukyu case and the question of Chinese merchants living mixed among Japanese were under discussion, Foreign Minister Inoue Kaoru held his ground very firmly; Shuchang argued back and forth repeatedly, and in the end matters proceeded as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: During talks on Ryukyu and Chinese merchants' residence rights, Foreign Minister Inoue Kaoru dug in hard; Shuchang debated him at length until the settlement went as planned.

sentences.zh: 明年，日本將襲朝鮮，庶昌電請速出援師為先發製人計。

translations.literal: The next year, when Japan was about to attack Korea, Shuchang telegraphed requesting that relief troops be dispatched swiftly as a preemptive strike.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, foreseeing a Japanese move against Korea, he wired Beijing urging prompt dispatch of forces to seize the initiative.

sentences.zh: 師至，日艦知有備，還，言歸於好。

translations.literal: When the troops arrived, the Japanese warships, knowing preparations had been made, withdrew, and both sides spoke of restored friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chinese forces appeared, Japanese ships, seeing they were expected, pulled back and both governments spoke of renewed amity.

sentences.zh: 中國古籍，經戎燼後多散佚，日籓族★L3藏富，庶昌擇其足翼經史者，刊古逸叢書二十六種。

translations.literal: China's ancient books, after the ravages of war, had largely scattered and been lost; Japanese clans held rich stores of books, and Shuchang selected those sufficient to supplement the classics and histories, publishing twenty-six titles in the Collection of Ancient Lost Texts.
translations.idiomatic: War had scattered many Chinese antiquarian texts, while Japanese collectors preserved rich libraries; Shuchang chose works that could bolster the classics and histories and issued twenty-six of them in the Guyi Congshu.

sentences.zh: 中法易約，條列七事進。

translations.literal: When the Sino-French treaty was revised, he submitted seven items in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At the revision of the Sino-French treaty he forwarded seven recommendations.

sentences.zh: 尋遭憂歸，服闋，仍故官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned home on bereavement leave; after mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home for mourning; when the period ended he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除川東道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed intendant of Eastern Sichuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891 he became intendant of Eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 川俗故闇僿。

translations.literal: Sichuan customs were formerly backward and uncultured.
translations.idiomatic: The province had long been provincial and insular.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，設學堂，倡實業，建病院，整武卹商，百廢具舉。

translations.literal: Once he took office, he founded schools, promoted practical industry, built hospitals, put military affairs in order and cared for merchants, and revived every neglected undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: In office he opened schools, fostered industry, built hospitals, tightened military administration, looked after merchants, and revived long-neglected projects across the board.

sentences.zh: 中東事起，庶昌曰：「日本蓄謀久矣，朝鮮猶其外府也。

translations.literal: When the First Sino-Japanese War broke out, Shuchang said: "Japan has long harbored designs; Korea is still its outer domain.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan erupted, Shuchang warned: "Japan has plotted for years; Korea is virtually its dependency.

sentences.zh: 戰固難勝，讓亦啟侮。」

translations.literal: To fight would be hard to win; to yield would invite contempt.
translations.idiomatic: We can hardly win a fight, yet concession will only invite further contempt.

sentences.zh: 乃倡佈告列邦議，以維持屬國，願東渡排難，當事者弗納。

translations.literal: Having closed his remarks, he thereupon proposed issuing a proclamation to the powers for joint deliberation to uphold the tributary state, and offered to cross eastward to mediate; those in charge did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged a circular note to the powers to uphold Korea's status and volunteered to go east to mediate; the leadership refused.

sentences.zh: 及戰事殷，財詘，庶昌首輸萬金，請按職列等差，亦不報。

translations.literal: When fighting intensified and funds ran short, Shuchang was first to donate ten thousand taels and requested that others contribute according to rank in graded amounts; this too received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: As the war deepened and coffers emptied, he gave ten thousand taels himself and asked officials to donate by rank; no answer came.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔陛見。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year an edict summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895 the court summoned him to audience.

sentences.zh: 駐渝法領事聞其將去，留辦教案，代者多方困之。

translations.literal: The French consul stationed in Chongqing, hearing he was about to leave, detained him to handle a missionary case, and his successor found many ways to obstruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The French consul in Chongqing, learning he was departing, kept him to settle a missionary dispute while his replacement worked to thwart him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 遘疾，遂去官。

translations.literal: He fell ill and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to leave office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 川東民建祠溈郡祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Eastern Sichuan built a shrine in Wei Prefecture to offer him sacrificial worship.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Sichuan locals erected a temple in the prefecture to honor him.

sentences.zh: 馬建忠，字眉叔，江蘇丹徒人。

translations.literal: Ma Jianzhong, style name Meishu, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jianzhong, courtesy name Meishu, came from Dantu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少好學，通經史。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He studied hard from boyhood and gained a firm command of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 憤外患日深，乃專究西學，派赴西洋各國使館學習洋務。

translations.literal: Angered that foreign threats grew daily deeper, he devoted himself to Western learning and was dispatched to study foreign affairs at embassies in various Western countries.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by mounting foreign pressure, he turned to Western learning and was sent to train at legations across Europe and America.

sentences.zh: 歷上書言借款、造路、創設海軍、通商、開礦、興學、儲材，北洋大臣李鴻章頗稱賞之，所議多采行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials on borrowing funds, building railways, creating a navy, expanding trade, opening mines, promoting schools, and stockpiling talent; Beiyang minister Li Hongzhang greatly praised him, and many of his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized repeatedly on loans, railways, a navy, trade, mining, education, and talent pools; Li Hongzhang admired his plans and put many into practice.

sentences.zh: 累保道員。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recommended for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was several times recommended for circuit-intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，鴻章遣建忠赴南洋與英人議鴉片專售事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, Hongzhang sent Jianzhong to Southeast Asia to negotiate with the British on the exclusive sale of opium.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 Li Hongzhang sent him to Southeast Asia to discuss British opium monopolies.

sentences.zh: 建忠以鴉片流毒，中外騰謗，當寓禁於徵，不可專重稅收。

translations.literal: Jianzhong held that opium's poisonous spread had stirred condemnation at home and abroad, and that prohibition should be embedded within taxation rather than relying solely on revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma argued that opium's harm had scandalized both countries, and that tax policy should serve suppression—not treat the drug chiefly as a revenue source.

sentences.zh: 時英人持正議者，亦以強開煙禁責其政府，引以為恥。

translations.literal: At the time upright British opinion also blamed their government for forcibly opening the opium trade, taking it as a shame.
translations.idiomatic: Even respectable British voices then condemned their government for imposing the opium trade and called it a national disgrace.

sentences.zh: 聞建忠言，雖未能遽許，皆稱其公。

translations.literal: Hearing Jianzhong's words, though they could not immediately agree, all praised his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: His British interlocutors could not commit at once, yet all praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝鮮始與美國議約，鴻章奏派建忠往蒞盟。
