translations.literal: In the eighth year Korea first negotiated a treaty with the United States; Hongzhang memorialized to dispatch Jianzhong to preside at the alliance ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882, when Korea opened treaty talks with the United States, Li Hongzhang sent Ma to oversee the signing.

sentences.zh: 約成，英、法先後遣使至，建忠介之，皆如美例成約。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded, Britain and France successively sent envoys; Jianzhong mediated, and all concluded treaties on the American model.
translations.idiomatic: After the American treaty, Britain and France followed; Ma brokered parallel agreements on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 日本駐朝公使屢诇結約事，建忠秘不使預聞，日人滋不悅。

translations.literal: The Japanese minister stationed in Korea repeatedly inquired about the treaty-making; Jianzhong kept it secret and did not let Japan participate, and the Japanese grew increasingly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Japan's minister in Seoul kept probing the negotiations; Ma kept Tokyo out, to growing Japanese irritation.

sentences.zh: 建忠歸而朝鮮亂作，庶昌以聞。

translations.literal: Jianzhong had just returned when unrest broke out in Korea, which Shuchang reported.
translations.idiomatic: Ma had barely returned when Korea erupted; Li Shuchang relayed the news.

sentences.zh: 時鴻章以憂去，張樹聲權北洋大臣，令建忠偕海軍提督丁汝昌率兵艦東渡觀變。

translations.literal: At that time Hongzhang had left office on bereavement; Zhang Shusheng acted as Beiyang minister and ordered Jianzhong together with naval commander Ding Ruchang to lead warships east across the sea to observe developments.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Hongzhang in mourning, acting Beiyang governor Zhang Shusheng sent Ma and Admiral Ding Ruchang east with warships to assess the crisis.

sentences.zh: 建忠抵仁川，日本海軍已先至，建忠設辭緩之，而亟請速濟師代定亂。

translations.literal: Jianzhong reached Incheon; the Japanese navy had already arrived first. Jianzhong used delaying talk to hold them off while urgently requesting that troops be sent quickly to quell the disorder on China's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: At Incheon he found the Japanese fleet already in port; he stalled with diplomacy while pressing Beijing to land troops and restore order.

sentences.zh: 朝命提督吳長慶率三千人東援。

translations.literal: The court ordered Commander Wu Changqing to lead three thousand men east in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing ordered General Wu Changqing east with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 建忠先定誘執首亂之策，偕長慶、汝昌往候大院君李昰應，減騶從，示坦率。

translations.literal: Jianzhong first settled on a plan to lure and seize the chief rebel; together with Changqing and Ruchang he went to wait upon Grand Prince Regent Yi Ha-ŭng, reducing his escort to show frankness.
translations.idiomatic: Ma devised a ruse to seize the rebellion's leader; with Wu and Ding he called on Grand Prince Regent Yi Ha-ŭng with a deliberately small escort to appear open-handed.

sentences.zh: 及昰應來報謁，建忠遂執之，強納諸輿，交長慶夜達兵輪，而汝昌護送至天津。

translations.literal: When Ha-ŭng came to return the visit, Jianzhong seized him, forced him into a palanquin, handed him to Changqing who by night reached the troopship, and Ruchang escorted him to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince returned the visit, Ma seized him, bundled him into a sedan, and had Wu rush him by night to a warship; Ding escorted him to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 复擒亂黨，援朝鮮國王復其位。

translations.literal: He again captured the rebels and supported the Korean king in restoring his throne.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel leaders were taken and the Korean king restored.

sentences.zh: 日使雖有言，而亂已定，亦無如何，皆建忠謀也。

translations.literal: Though the Japanese minister had words to say, the disorder was already settled and nothing could be done—all was Jianzhong's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese minister protested, but with order restored he could do little—it was Ma's doing throughout.

sentences.zh: 於是長慶統軍留駐，其隨員袁世凱始來佐營務。

translations.literal: Thereupon Changqing remained with his army stationed there, and his staff member Yuan Shikai first came to assist with camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changqing then garrisoned Korea, and a young Yuan Shikai joined his staff for the first time.

sentences.zh: 及建忠歸，而維新黨之亂又作。

translations.literal: By the time Jianzhong returned, the Gapsin Coup unrest had broken out again.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ma got home, the Gapsin reformers' coup had already flared anew.

sentences.zh: 日軍先入，交涉屢失機，其後卒致全敗。

translations.literal: Japanese troops entered first; negotiations repeatedly missed their moment, and in the end total defeat ensued.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese forces moved in first; diplomacy fumbled chance after chance, and the later collapse followed.

sentences.zh: 建忠憤後繼失人，初謀盡毀，譔東行錄以記其事。

translations.literal: Jianzhong resented that successors had lost the right men and the original plans were utterly ruined; he compiled the Record of the Eastern Mission to recount these events.
translations.idiomatic: Bitter that later hands squandered his strategy, he wrote the Dongxing lu to record what had been lost.

sentences.zh: 建忠博學，善古文辭；

translations.literal: Jianzhong was broadly learned and skilled at classical prose;
translations.idiomatic: Ma was erudite and a strong classical stylist;

sentences.zh: 尤精歐文，自英、法現行文字以至希臘、拉丁古文，無不兼通。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in European writing, from current English and French to ancient Greek and Latin, mastering all without exception.
translations.idiomatic: and exceptionally fluent in European languages—from modern English and French to ancient Greek and Latin.

sentences.zh: 以泰西各國皆有學文程式之書，中文經籍雖皆有規矩隱寓其中，特無有為之比儗而揭示之，遂使學者論文困於句解，知其然而不能知其所以然。

translations.literal: Because every Western country had books setting forth the rules of literary composition, whereas Chinese classics also contained implicit norms but lacked a comparable work to lay them bare, learners discussing prose remained trapped in line-by-line glossing, knowing the what but not the why.
translations.idiomatic: Western nations all had explicit grammars of style, while Chinese texts hid their rules in usage without a guide to expose them—leaving students able to parse lines yet unable to grasp underlying principles.

sentences.zh: 乃發憤創為文通一書，因西文已有之規矩，於經籍中求其所同所不同者，曲證繁引，以確知中文義例之所在，務令學者明所區別，而後施之於文，各得其當，不唯執筆學為古文詞有左宜右有之妙，即學泰西古今一切文學，亦不難精求而會通焉。

translations.literal: He therefore resolved in indignation to create the book Wen Tong; applying rules already established in Western writing, he sought in the classics what matched and what differed, arguing at length with abundant citation to fix where Chinese usage truly lay, so that learners would understand the distinctions and then apply them in writing each in its proper place—not only gaining the left-right fitting subtlety of composing classical prose, but also finding it no hard matter to pursue and harmonize all Western literature ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: In response he wrote Wen Tong, mapping Western rhetorical rules onto the Chinese canon—what aligned, what diverged—so students could see why prose works as it does, write with precision in the classical mode, and even approach Western literatures with confidence.

sentences.zh: 書出，學者皆稱其精，推為古今特創之作。

translations.literal: When the book appeared, scholars all praised its refinement and hailed it as an unprecedented work of its kind through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: On publication scholars acclaimed its rigor and called it a path-breaking work.

sentences.zh: 又著有適可齋記言、記行等書。

translations.literal: He also authored Records of Discourse from the Shike Studio, Travel Records, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He also left Shike Studio jiyan, jixing, and related writings.

sentences.zh: 李鳳苞，字丹厓，江蘇崇明人。

translations.literal: Li Fengbao, style name Danya, was a native of Chongming in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengbao, courtesy name Danya, came from Chongming in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧，究心曆算之學，精測繪。

translations.literal: From youth he was intelligent; he devoted himself to calendrical calculation and excelled at surveying and mapping.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as a boy, he pursued astronomy and mathematics and became an expert surveyor.

sentences.zh: 丁日昌撫吳，知其才，資以貲為道員。

translations.literal: When Ding Richang governed Jiangsu, recognizing his talent, he funded his advancement to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ding Richang spotted his ability, backed him financially, and helped him reach circuit-intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 歷辦江南製造局、吳淞砲台工程局，繪地球全圖，並譯西洋諸書。

translations.literal: He successively managed the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Wusong Fort Engineering Bureau, drew a complete map of the globe, and translated various Western books.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the Jiangnan Arsenal and Wusong fort works, produced a world map, and translated Western texts.

sentences.zh: 日昌為船政大臣，調充總考工。

translations.literal: When Richang became superintendent of naval affairs, Fengbao was transferred to serve as chief examiner of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding took charge of the Fuzhou shipyard, Li became chief engineering examiner.

sentences.zh: 朝議遣生徒出洋，加三品卿，派為監督。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated sending students abroad, he was granted third-rank minister rank and appointed superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: As China prepared to send students overseas, he received third-rank rank and was named superintendent.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，率赴英、法兩國，分置肆業。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he led them to Britain and France and placed them to pursue their studies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he escorted the cohort to Britain and France and set them to their studies.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜二品頂戴，​​充出使德國大臣，旋兼使奧、義、荷三國，往來數千里，周旋各國間，聯絡邦交。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted second-rank courtier insignia and appointed minister to Germany, soon concurrently minister to Austria, Italy, and the Netherlands as well, traveling thousands of li among the states and cultivating diplomatic ties.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received second-rank insignia and became minister to Germany, later adding Austria, Italy, and the Netherlands—crisscrossing thousands of miles to strengthen relations.

sentences.zh: 時建議興海軍，並命督造戰艦。

translations.literal: At the time a plan to build a navy was under discussion, and he was also ordered to supervise construction of warships.
translations.idiomatic: Naval expansion was then on the agenda, and he was told to oversee warship construction as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越構釁，暫署法使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when France and Vietnam clashed, he temporarily acted as minister to France.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, amid the Franco-Vietnamese crisis, he briefly served as minister to France.

sentences.zh: 法事決裂，遂奉命回國，歸過澳門。

translations.literal: When relations with France broke down, he was ordered to return home, passing through Macau on the way.
translations.idiomatic: After the break with France he was recalled, stopping in Macau en route.

sentences.zh: 澳門自明中葉久為葡萄牙人稅居，及是葡人私議欲攘為己有。

translations.literal: Macau since the mid-Ming had long been leased to the Portuguese for taxation residence; at this time the Portuguese privately discussed seizing it as their own.
translations.idiomatic: Macau had been under Portuguese lease since the mid-Ming; now Lisbon quietly debated annexing it outright.

sentences.zh: 鳳苞寓書部臣，乞請旨與葡人定約，免後患。

translations.literal: Fengbao sent a letter to the ministry, begging that an imperial order be sought to fix a treaty with the Portuguese and avert future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Li wrote the Board urging an imperial mandate to negotiate with Portugal before trouble arose.

sentences.zh: 部臣懼生事，寢其議。

translations.literal: The ministry feared provoking trouble and shelved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fearing a flare-up let the idea die.

sentences.zh: 後一年，葡人遂據其地，論者惜之。

translations.literal: A year later the Portuguese then occupied the territory; commentators regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Portugal seized the enclave—to later regret among observers.

sentences.zh: 既，覆命，有旨發往直隸交李鴻章差遣，令總辦營務處，兼管水師學堂。

translations.literal: Afterward, upon reporting back, an edict ordered him sent to Zhili under Li Hongzhang's command, placed in charge of the military affairs bureau and concurrently managing the naval academy.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was posted to Zhili under Li Hongzhang to head military affairs and the naval academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以在德造艦報銷不實，被議革職。

translations.literal: Before long, because shipbuilding accounts in Germany were found inaccurate, he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon irregularities in German ship accounts led to his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1887.

sentences.zh: 著有四裔編年表、西國政聞彙編、文藻齋詩文集等。

translations.literal: He authored the Annals of the Four Borderlands, Compilations of Western Political News, and the Wen Zao Studio collected poetry and prose, among other works.
translations.idiomatic: His publications include the Siyi biannian biao, Xiguo zhengwen huibian, and Wen Zao Studio collected works.

sentences.zh: 其他音韻、地理、數學，皆有論著，未成。

translations.literal: On phonology, geography, and mathematics as well he had treatises, but they were never completed.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted works on phonology, geography, and mathematics that remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 洪鈞，字文卿，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Hong Jun, style name Wenqing, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Jun, courtesy name Wenqing, came from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 同治七年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he placed first in the metropolitan examination as lead jinshi and was appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he topped the jinshi list as zhuangyuan and entered the Hanlin Academy as compiler.

sentences.zh: 出督湖北學政，歷典陝西、山東鄉試。

translations.literal: He went out as educational commissioner of Hubei and successively presided over the provincial examinations of Shaanxi and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Hubei education commissioner and later chief examiner for Shaanxi and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 遷侍讀，視學江西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to reader-in-waiting and served as educational inspector of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to reader-in-waiting, he inspected schools in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，歷遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he was promoted through posts to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: By 1881 he had risen to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 母老乞終養，嗣丁憂，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: His mother was aged and he requested leave to care for her until death; afterward he entered mourning; when mourning ended he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He sought leave to nurse his elderly mother, then mourned her death; after mourning he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 出使俄德奧比四國大臣，晉兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as minister to Russia, Germany, Austria, and Belgium, and was promoted to vice minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He became envoy to Russia, Germany, Austria, and Belgium and rose to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 初，喀什噶爾續勘西邊界約，中國圖學未精，乏善本。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Kashgar supplementary survey of the western boundary treaty was undertaken, Chinese cartography was not advanced and lacked good maps.
translations.idiomatic: When Kashgar's western border was re-surveyed under treaty, China lacked reliable maps and skilled cartographers.

sentences.zh: 鈞蒞俄，以俄人所訂中俄界圖紅線均與界約符，私慮英先發，乃譯成漢字備不虞。

translations.literal: When Jun arrived in Russia, because the red lines on the Sino-Russian boundary map drawn by the Russians all accorded with the border treaty, he privately feared Britain would move first, and so had it translated into Chinese characters against unforeseen contingencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Russia he found the red lines on Moscow's Sino-Russian map matched the treaty; fearing Britain might act first, he had the chart rendered in Chinese as a safeguard.

sentences.zh: 十六年，使成​​，攜之歸，命直總理各國事務衙門。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the mission was completed; he brought it back and was ordered to serve directly at the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1890 the work was finished; he returned with the map and was posted directly to the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 值帕米爾爭界事起，大理寺少卿延茂謂鈞所譯地圖畫蘇滿諸卡置界外，致邊事日棘，乃痛劾其貽誤狀，事下總署察覆。

translations.literal: Just as the Pamir boundary dispute arose, Yan Mao, vice president of the Dali Court, said that Jun's translated map placed the Sum checkpoints outside the border, causing frontier affairs to grow daily more urgent; he therefore bitterly impeached him for causing harm, and the matter was referred to the Zongli Yamen for investigation and report.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pamir border dispute flared up, Vice President Yan Mao of the Dali Court charged that Jun's translated map had drawn the Sum outposts beyond China's line, worsening the frontier crisis. He filed a sharp impeachment, and the case went to the Zongli Yamen for review.

sentences.zh: 總署同列諸臣以鈞所譯圖，本以備考覈，非以為左證，且非專為中俄交涉而設，安得歸咎於此圖？

translations.literal: Colleagues at the Zongli Yamen held that Jun's translated map was originally for reference and verification, not to serve as evidence, and was not made specifically for Sino-Russian negotiations—how could blame be laid on this map?
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues at the Yamen replied that Jun's chart had been meant for reference, not as legal proof, and was never drawn solely for the Russian talks—so the map could hardly be blamed.

sentences.zh: 事白，而言者猶未息。

translations.literal: The matter was cleared, yet those who spoke against him still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He was cleared, but his critics would not let the affair drop.

sentences.zh: 右庶子準良建議，帕地圖說紛紜，宜求精確。

translations.literal: Right Sub-Reader Zhun Liang proposed that Pamir maps and accounts were confused and that accuracy should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Right Sub-Reader Zhun Liang urged that Pamir cartography was a tangle of conflicting accounts and ought to be corrected.

sentences.zh: 於是鈞等具疏論列，謂：「內府輿圖、一統誌圖紀載漏略。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun and others submitted a memorial setting forth their views, saying: "The palace atlases and the maps in the Comprehensive Gazetteer are incomplete in their records.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and his colleagues then memorialized the throne, arguing that "the palace atlases and the maps in the Comprehensive Gazetteer are full of gaps.

sentences.zh: 總署歷辦此案，證以李鴻章譯寄英圖，與許景澄集成英、俄、德、法全圖，無大紕繆，而覈諸準良所奏，則歧異甚多。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen has handled this case throughout, verifying it against the British map Li Hongzhang translated and sent, and the complete British, Russian, German, and French map Xu Jingcheng assembled—without major error—yet checked against what Zhun Liang memorialized, the discrepancies are very many.
translations.idiomatic: In handling the case the Yamen had checked Jun's work against Li Hongzhang's translated British chart and Xu Jingcheng's composite map of Britain, Russia, Germany, and France and found no serious mistakes—yet compared with Zhun Liang's memorial, the differences were numerous.

sentences.zh: 欽定西域圖誌敘霍爾幹諸地，則總結之曰屬喀什噶爾；

translations.literal: The imperially authorized Western Regions Gazetteer, in treating Khorgan and other places, summarizes by saying they belong to Kashgar;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial Western Regions Gazetteer describes Khorgan and neighboring districts and plainly concludes that they belong to Kashgar;

sentences.zh: 敘喇楚勒、葉什勒庫勒諸地，則總結之曰屬喀什噶爾西境外：文義明顯。

translations.literal: in treating Lachu, Yeshilku, and other places, it summarizes by saying they lie outside the western border of Kashgar—the meaning of the text is clear.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Lachu, Yeshilku, and the like it sums up as lying beyond Kashgar's western frontier—the wording is unmistakable.

sentences.zh: 原奏乃謂：'其曰境外者，大小和卓木舊境外也。

translations.literal: The original memorial nevertheless says: 'Where it says "outside the border," it means outside the old domain of the Khoja brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier memorial, however, claims: 'When the text says "outside the border," it means outside the old Khoja domain.

sentences.zh: 曰屬者，屬今喀什噶爾，為國家自闢之壤地也。

translations.literal: Where it says "belonging," it means belonging to present-day Kashgar, land opened by the state itself.
translations.idiomatic: Where it says "belonging," it means today's Kashgar—territory the dynasty itself had opened.

sentences.zh: '語近穿鑿。

translations.literal: The language comes close to forced interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: That reading is far-fetched.

sentences.zh: 喀地正北、東北毗俄七河，正西倚俄費爾幹，其西南錯居者帕也。

translations.literal: Kashgar territory on the due north and northeast adjoins Russia's Seven Rivers region; due west it leans on Russian Ferghana; to the southwest, interspersed among them, lies the Pamir.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar's north and northeast border Russian Semirechye; its west rests on Russian Ferghana; and the Pamir lies interleaved to the southwest.

sentences.zh: 後藏極西曰阿里，西北循雪山迳挪格爾、坎巨提，訖印度克什米爾，無待北涉帕地。

translations.literal: The western extremity of rear Tibet is called Ali; northwestward one follows snow mountains through Nagar and Kanjut to Indian Kashmir, with no need to go north through Pamir territory.
translations.idiomatic: Far western Tibet is Ali; from there one can reach Indian Kashmir northwest along the snow ranges through Nagar and Kanjut without crossing the Pamir at all.

sentences.zh: 設俄欲躡喀，英欲偪阿里，不患無路。

translations.literal: Suppose Russia wished to encroach on Kashgar or Britain wished to press upon Ali—they need not worry about lacking a route.
translations.idiomatic: If Russia meant to move on Kashgar or Britain to pressure Ali, routes existed aplenty.

sentences.zh: 原奏乃謂：'二國侵奪拔達克山、安集延而終莫得通。

translations.literal: The original memorial nevertheless says: 'The two countries seized Badakhshan and Andijan yet in the end could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the earlier memorial insists: 'Russia and Britain seized Badakhshan and Andijan and still could not break through.

sentences.zh: '斯於邊情不亦闇乎？

translations.literal: Is this not blindness to frontier conditions?
translations.idiomatic: Surely that shows ignorance of the border situation.

sentences.zh: 中俄分界，起科布多、塔爾巴哈台、伊犁，訖喀西南烏仔別里山口止，並自東北以達西南。

translations.literal: The Sino-Russian boundary runs from Kobdo, Tarbagatai, and Ili to the Uz Beli pass southwest of Kashgar, all traced from northeast to southwest.
translations.idiomatic: The Sino-Russian line runs from Kobdo, Tarbagatai, and Ili to the Uz Beli pass southwest of Kashgar, drawn consistently from northeast to southwest.

sentences.zh: 原奏乃謂：'當日勘界，自俄屬薩馬干而東，實以烏仔別里西口為界。

translations.literal: The original memorial nevertheless says: 'When the boundary was surveyed at the time, from Russian Samarkand eastward, the western mouth of Uz Beli was in fact taken as the border.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier memorial claims: 'The survey began east from Russian Samarkand and fixed the border at the western mouth of Uz Beli.

sentences.zh: 今斷以東口，大乖情勢。

translations.literal: Now fixing it at the eastern mouth greatly departs from the actual circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: To draw the line at the eastern mouth now would grossly distort the facts.

sentences.zh: '案各城約無薩馬干地名，惟浩罕、安集延極西有薩馬爾幹，明史作撒馬兒罕，久隸俄，與我疆無涉。

translations.literal: On investigation, none of the Khorasan treaties contains the place-name Samarkand; only at the far west of Kokand and Andijan is Samarqand, written in the Ming History as Samarqand, long subject to Russia and unrelated to our territory.
translations.idiomatic: No treaty of the period mentions Samarkand; there is only Samarqand far west in Kokand and Andijan—the Ming History's Samarqand—long under Russia and irrelevant to our frontier.

sentences.zh: 當日勘界，並非自西而東，亦無東西二口之說，不知原奏何以傳訛若此？

translations.literal: The boundary survey at the time was not from west to east, nor is there any doctrine of eastern and western mouths—one does not know why the original memorial transmitted such error?
translations.idiomatic: The survey was never run from west to east, nor was there ever talk of two mouths of the pass—how the earlier memorial came to repeat such errors is unclear.

sentences.zh: 謹繪許景澄所寄地圖以進。」

translations.literal: Respectfully we have drawn the map Xu Jingcheng sent and submit it."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully submit a map drawn from the chart Xu Jingcheng provided."

sentences.zh: 並陳扼守蔥嶺及爭蘇滿有礙約章狀。

translations.literal: They also set forth the situation regarding holding the Pamir passes and contesting Sum in conflict with treaty provisions.
translations.idiomatic: They also explained why holding the Pamir highlands and pressing Sum ran counter to existing treaties.

sentences.zh: 先是坎巨提之役，彼此​​爭惎其間，我是以有退兵撤卡之舉，英乘隙而使阿富汗據蘇滿。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Kanjut campaign, both sides nursed mutual grievances between them; we therefore withdrew troops and removed checkpoints, and Britain seized the opportunity to have Afghanistan occupy Sum.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Kanjut affair, mutual suspicion had poisoned relations; China withdrew troops and dismantled outposts, and Britain used the opening to place Afghanistan in Sum.

sentences.zh: 至是，俄西隊出與阿戰，東隊且駸駸偪邊境。

translations.literal: By this time Russia's western column had gone out to fight the Afghans, and its eastern column was steadily pressing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Now Russia's western force was fighting the Afghans while its eastern column pressed ever closer to the border.

sentences.zh: 總署复具籌辦西南邊外本末以上。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen again submitted a full account of how the southwestern frontier beyond the border had been handled.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen again laid before the throne a full history of southwestern frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 鈞附言：「自譯中俄界圖，知烏仔別里以南，東西橫亙，皆是帕地。

translations.literal: Jun added in a postscript: "From translating the Sino-Russian boundary map, I know that south of Uz Beli, spanning east and west, all is Pamir territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jun added: "Translating the Sino-Russian boundary map showed me that everything south of Uz Beli, stretching east to west, is Pamir country.

sentences.zh: 喀約所謂中國界線，應介乎其間。

translations.literal: The Chinese boundary line mentioned in the Kashgar treaty ought to lie between them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese line stipulated in the Kashgar treaty should run between these zones.

sentences.zh: 今日俄人爭帕，早種因喀城定約之年。

translations.literal: Today's Russian contest for the Pamir was seeded long ago in the year the Kashgar treaty was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Russia's present bid for the Pamir was planted when the Kashgar treaty was signed.

sentences.zh: 劉錦棠添設蘇卡，意在拓邊。

translations.literal: Liu Jintang's addition of Sum checkpoints was intended to expand the border.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jintang had added Sum outposts to push the frontier outward.

sentences.zh: 無如喀約具在，成事難說。

translations.literal: But the Kashgar treaty stands complete, and the accomplished fact is hard to explain away.
translations.idiomatic: But the Kashgar treaty remained in force, making the fait accompli hard to defend.

sentences.zh: 唯依界圖南北經度斜線，自烏仔別裡徑南，尚可得帕地少半，尋按故址，已稍廓張。

translations.literal: Only by following the north-south diagonal of longitude on the boundary map, straight south from Uz Beli, can somewhat more than half the Pamir still be obtained; searching out old sites, the area has already been slightly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Following the boundary map's diagonal meridian due south from Uz Beli, China could still claim somewhat more than half the Pamir; by reoccupying old sites, the claim had already been modestly enlarged.

sentences.zh: 俄阿交閧，揣阿必潰。

translations.literal: Russia and Afghanistan are clashing; I surmise the Afghans will collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Russia and Afghanistan were at odds, and he expected the Afghans to break.

sentences.zh: 俟俄退兵，可與議界，當更與疆臣合力經營，爭得一分即獲一分之益。」

translations.literal: Wait until Russia withdraws its troops, then boundary talks may be held; one should work jointly with frontier officials, and every foot gained will bring a foot's benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Once Russia pulled back, negotiations could begin; working with frontier officials, every inch secured would be an inch gained."

sentences.zh: 上皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every point.

sentences.zh: 十九年，卒，予優恤。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died and was granted special mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: In 1893 he died and received exceptional posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 鈞嗜學，通經史，嘗譔元史釋文證補，取材域外，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Jun loved learning and mastered the classics and history; he once compiled textual notes, evidence, and supplements to the Yuan History, drawing on foreign sources, and contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was a devoted scholar of the classics and history; his Yuan History: Notes, Evidence, and Supplements drew on foreign materials and won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 劉瑞芬，字芝田，安徽貴池人。

translations.literal: Liu Ruifen, style name Zhitian, was a native of Guichi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ruifen, courtesy name Zhitian, came from Guichi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以諸生從李鴻章軍援上海，檄主水陸軍械轉運。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he followed Li Hongzhang's army to relieve Shanghai and was ordered to manage transport of ordnance by land and sea.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he joined Li Hongzhang's force sent to relieve Shanghai and was put in charge of moving arms and supplies by land and sea.

sentences.zh: 時初用西式槍砲，皆購自外洋，瑞芬考驗精審，應時解濟，淮軍遂以善用西洋利器名。

translations.literal: At the time Western-style muskets and cannon were first used, all purchased abroad; Ruifen examined them meticulously and delivered supplies on schedule, and the Huai Army thus became famed for skill with Western weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Western rifles and cannon were then new, all bought overseas; Ruifen inspected them carefully and kept deliveries on time, earning the Huai Army its reputation for mastering foreign arms.

sentences.zh: 累保道員，督辦松滬釐捐。

translations.literal: Through repeated recommendations he rose to circuit intendant and supervised the Songhu likin.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted repeatedly to circuit intendant, he oversaw the Songhu likin.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，權兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he served as acting salt transport commissioner of the Liang-Huai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he acted as Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮北薦飢，流民就食揚州，瑞芬築圩城外，構棚分宿，計口授食，所全活六萬餘人。

translations.literal: When north Huai suffered repeated famine, refugees came to Yangzhou for food; Ruifen built dikes outside the city, erected sheds for separate lodging, and distributed food by head count, saving more than sixty thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in north Huai, refugees flooded Yangzhou; Ruifen built dikes and shelters outside the walls, rationed food by head, and kept more than sixty thousand people alive.

sentences.zh: 旋授蘇松太道。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed intendant of the Suzhou-Songjiang-Shanghai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made intendant of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 租界以黃浦南北分華洋船埠，洋人時侵南岸。

translations.literal: The concession divided Chinese and foreign wharves north and south of the Huangpu, and foreigners often encroached on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: The concession split wharves on the north and south banks of the Huangpu between Chinese and foreign use, and foreigners repeatedly encroached on the south shore.

sentences.zh: 瑞芬丈量南北，中分為界，設水利局委員董其事，洋人亦就範焉。

translations.literal: Ruifen measured north and south, divided the middle as the boundary, and established Water Conservancy Bureau commissioners to oversee the matter; foreigners also submitted to the arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Ruifen surveyed both banks, fixed a central boundary, and put Water Conservancy Bureau commissioners in charge; the foreigners complied.

sentences.zh: 擢江西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge of Jiangxi and transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Jiangxi provincial judge and then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十一年，改三品京堂，命充出使英俄等國大臣；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was changed to a third-rank Beijing official and appointed minister to Britain, Russia, and other countries;
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he became a third-rank Beijing official and was appointed envoy to Britain, Russia, and other powers;

sentences.zh: 授太常寺卿，遷大理寺，仍留使。

translations.literal: he was appointed vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, transferred to the Dali Court, and still retained his post as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: named vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then of the Dali Court while remaining in his post abroad.

sentences.zh: 改駐英、法、義、比。

translations.literal: His posting was changed to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium.
translations.idiomatic: His mission was reassigned to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium.

sentences.zh: 初，俄人覬覦漠河金礦，瑞芬亟達總理衙門，創議先自開辦。

translations.literal: Initially, when Russians coveted the Mohe gold mines, Ruifen urgently reported to the Zongli Yamen and proposed that China open them first itself.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia cast covetous eyes on the Mohe goldfields, Ruifen urged the Zongli Yamen to develop them before anyone else could.

sentences.zh: 英既佔緬甸，罷其朝貢，瑞芬執故事與爭，仍如舊。

translations.literal: After Britain occupied Burma and abolished its tribute missions, Ruifen argued from precedent and tribute continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Britain annexed Burma and tried to end its tribute missions, Ruifen invoked precedent and kept the old arrangement intact.

sentences.zh: 英复侵西藏，瑞芬力爭於其外部，追還印度入藏之師，乃別議藏印條約，事具邦交志。

translations.literal: Britain again invaded Tibet; Ruifen argued forcefully at its Foreign Office, recalled the Indian troops entering Tibet, and then separately negotiated a Tibet-India treaty—the details are in the diplomatic annals.
translations.idiomatic: When Britain moved on Tibet again, Ruifen pressed its Foreign Office hard, secured the withdrawal of Indian troops, and helped negotiate a separate Tibet-India treaty, as recorded in the diplomatic annals.

sentences.zh: 瑞芬久事​​外交，有遠見。

translations.literal: Ruifen had long served in foreign affairs and possessed foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Long experienced in diplomacy, Ruifen was a man of foresight.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮亂初起，即上書言：「朝鮮毗連東三省，關係甚重。

translations.literal: When the Korean unrest first broke out, he immediately submitted a memorial saying: "Korea adjoins the three eastern provinces and the relationship is very important.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble first erupted in Korea, he memorialized at once: "Korea borders the three eastern provinces; the stakes are immense.

sentences.zh: 中國能收其全土改行省，上策也。

translations.literal: If China can take its entire territory and make it a province, that is the best policy.
translations.idiomatic: The best course would be to annex the whole country and make it a province.

sentences.zh: 次則當約英、美諸國共議保護，庶免強鄰獨占，存籓屬以固邊陲。」

translations.literal: Next best is to invite Britain, America, and other countries to discuss joint protection, so that a strong neighbor may not occupy it alone, preserving vassal status to secure the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, China should enlist Britain, America, and others in joint protection to keep a single power from seizing it, preserving the tributary tie to guard the frontier."

sentences.zh: 總署寢其議不行，其後果如所言。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen shelved his proposal and did not act on it; afterward events proved exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The Yamen shelved the plan, and events later unfolded just as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 十五年，召授廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled and appointed governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1889 he was recalled and appointed governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died; mourning honors followed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1892 and received the standard mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 子三。

translations.literal: He had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 世珩，字聚卿。

translations.literal: Shihang, style name Juqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shihang, courtesy name Juqing.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 累至道員。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 歷辦江南商務官報、學務工程、湖北造幣等事。

translations.literal: He successively handled the Jiangnan Commercial Gazette, education and engineering projects, Hubei coin minting, and other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Jiangnan Commercial Gazette, education and engineering projects, the Hubei mint, and other offices.

sentences.zh: 旋擢度支部參議，加三品卿。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to counsellor of the Ministry of Revenue and granted third-rank noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a counsellor in the Ministry of Revenue with third-rank noble rank.

sentences.zh: 條議幣制，中外稱其精確，未及行而辛亥變起，遂歸寓上海。

translations.literal: He drafted proposals on the currency system; Chinese and foreigners alike praised their precision, but before they could be implemented the Xinhai uprising broke out, and he retired to live in Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: His currency proposals won praise at home and abroad, but the Xinhai Revolution intervened before they could be enacted, and he settled in Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 丙寅年，卒。

translations.literal: In the bingyin year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1926.

sentences.zh: 嗜古，富藏書，校刊古籍尤精。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity, possessed a rich library, and was especially skilled at collating ancient texts.
translations.idiomatic: A collector and bibliophile, he was especially adept at collating rare editions.

sentences.zh: 有聚學軒叢書、貴池先哲遺書、玉海堂宋元槧本叢書及曲譜、曲品等。

translations.literal: He published the Juxue Studio Collectanea, Posthumous Works of Guichi Worthies, the Yuhai Studio Song-Yuan Woodblock Collectanea, and works on music scores and drama criticism, among others.
translations.idiomatic: His publications include the Juxue Studio Collectanea, Posthumous Works of Guichi Worthies, the Yuhai Studio Song-Yuan woodblock series, and studies of music and drama.

sentences.zh: 徐壽朋，字進齋，直隸清苑人，本籍浙江紹興。

translations.literal: Xu Shoupeng, style name Jinzhai, was a native of Qingyuan in Zhili, with ancestral registration in Shaoxing, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shoupeng, courtesy name Jinzhai, was registered in Qingyuan, Zhili, though his family came from Shaoxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以廩貢生納貲為主事。

translations.literal: By purchased degree as a tribute student from the granary quota he became a secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as a secretary through the tribute-student route.

sentences.zh: 諳習外情，佐津海關辦交涉。

translations.literal: Well versed in foreign conditions, he assisted the Tianjin Customs in handling diplomatic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in foreign affairs, he assisted the Tianjin Customs with diplomacy.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，以道員充美日使館二等參贊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, as circuit intendant he served as second secretary at the American and Japanese legations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he went abroad as second secretary at the American and Japanese legations, holding circuit-intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 時華人傭於洛士丙冷者多被虐殺，壽朋佐使臣鄭藻如索償，詞錚義屈。

translations.literal: At the time many Chinese laborers employed at Rock Springs were massacred; Shoupeng assisted Minister Zheng Zaoru in demanding compensation, his words sharp and his righteousness prevailing.
translations.idiomatic: When Chinese miners at Rock Springs were massacred, Shoupeng helped Envoy Zheng Zaoru demand compensation, arguing with force until justice prevailed.

sentences.zh: 未竟，會開秘魯使館，移充駐秘參贊，攝行公使事。

translations.literal: Before the matter was finished, a Peruvian legation was opened; he was transferred to serve as secretary in Peru and acted in the minister's place.
translations.idiomatic: Before that case closed, China opened a legation in Peru; he was posted there as secretary and acted as minister.

sentences.zh: 秘故虐遇華工，益苛其例，壽朋與秘廷辨論，多所補救。

translations.literal: Peru had long mistreated Chinese workers and further tightened its regulations; Shoupeng debated with the Peruvian court and remedied many abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Peru had long abused Chinese laborers and tightened its rules; Shoupeng argued with the government and won substantial relief.

sentences.zh: 駐外久，辦理交涉，常服遠人。

translations.literal: Long stationed abroad, in handling diplomacy he often won over foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: Years abroad had taught him to handle negotiations in ways foreigners respected.

sentences.zh: 晉二品秩。

translations.literal: He was promoted to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to second rank.

sentences.zh: 還國，適李鴻章督畿輔，闢居幕府。

translations.literal: Returning home, just as Li Hongzhang was governing the metropolitan region, he was invited to join his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Back in China, he entered Li Hongzhang's staff when Li became governor-general of the metropolitan provinces.

sentences.zh: 疏薦其練吏治，熟邦交。

translations.literal: Li memorialized recommending him as skilled in administration and versed in foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: Li recommended him as an able administrator with deep knowledge of foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 召見，奏對稱旨。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, his memorial answers pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he answered to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授安徽徽寧池太廣道，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed intendant of the Huining-Chizhou-Taizhou-Guangde circuit in Anhui and promoted to provincial judge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was made intendant of Anhui's Huining-Chizhou-Taizhou-Guangde circuit and then provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 未半載，徵還，命以三品京堂充韓國全權議約大臣。

translations.literal: Before half a year had passed he was recalled and ordered, as a third-rank Beijing official, to serve as plenipotentiary treaty minister to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Within six months he was recalled and sent to Korea as plenipotentiary treaty commissioner, holding third-rank Beijing rank.

sentences.zh: 既至，與其外部樸齊純議定商約十三條，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he negotiated thirteen commercial articles with Foreign Minister Pak Je-sun; the details are in the diplomatic annals.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he negotiated thirteen commercial articles with Foreign Minister Pak Je-sun, as recorded in the diplomatic annals.

sentences.zh: 初，韓本為我屬國，貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Initially Korea had been our vassal state, its tribute missions unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Korea had long been a tributary state sending regular missions.

sentences.zh: 自馬關定新約，認為獨立自主，遂以壽朋膺使命，是為中韓立約之始。

translations.literal: Since the Shimonoseki treaty recognized it as independent and autonomous, Shoupeng was entrusted with the mission—this was the beginning of Sino-Korean treaty relations.
translations.idiomatic: After Shimonoseki recognized Korean independence, Shoupeng's mission marked the start of formal Sino-Korean treaty relations.

sentences.zh: 其秋，除太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was named vice president of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 約成，改充出使韓國大臣。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded, he was changed to minister to Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Once the treaty was signed, he became minister to Korea.

sentences.zh: 奏設漢城總領事，惠保僑民，始復自治權。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish a consul-general at Seoul to protect overseas Chinese, restoring their autonomous jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: He established a consul-general in Seoul to protect Chinese residents and restore their self-governing rights.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，聯軍入京，鴻章被命議和，奏調壽朋佐議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the allied armies entered Beijing; Hongzhang was ordered to negotiate peace and memorialized to transfer Shoupeng to assist in the talks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the allied armies occupied Beijing; Li Hongzhang was charged with peace talks and summoned Shoupeng to assist.

sentences.zh: 壽朋習西國語言文字，徐起應付，卒能不失鴻章本意。

translations.literal: Shoupeng was versed in Western languages and writing; he responded deliberately and in the end did not depart from Hongzhang's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in Western languages, Shoupeng handled the negotiations carefully and never lost sight of Li Hongzhang's aims.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，議定和約十二款。

translations.literal: After more than a year, a twelve-article peace treaty was settled.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later they finalized a twelve-article peace treaty.

sentences.zh: 复力請回鑾。

translations.literal: He again vigorously petitioned for the court's return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed hard for the court to return to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 遷外務部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice President of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left vice president of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，予優恤。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness and was granted special mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died, receiving exceptional posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 楊儒，字子通，漢軍正紅旗入。

translations.literal: Yang Ru, style name Zitong, entered the civil service from the Han Banner of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ru, courtesy name Zitong, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 以監生納貲為員外郎，銓兵部。

translations.literal: By purchased degree as a student he became a department secretary and was assigned to the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: He bought office as a department secretary and was posted to the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 舉同治六年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the sixth year of Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations in 1867.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為常鎮道。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as intendant of Chang-Zhen circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was appointed intendant of the Chang-Zhen circuit.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋，除溫處道，調徽寧池太道。

translations.literal: Upon his mother’s death he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed intendant of Wen-Chu circuit and transferred to intendant of Huai-Ning-Chi-Tai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he took up the Wen-Chu intendant post, then moved to the Huai-Ning-Chi-Tai circuit.

sentences.zh: 光緒十八年，改四品卿，出使美日秘三國大臣，補太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he was changed to fourth-rank grand secretary, minister to the United States, Japan, and Peru, and appointed vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1892 he became a fourth-rank grand secretary and envoy to the United States, Japan, and Peru, while also serving as vice president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 與英外部葛禮山續定華工條約。

translations.literal: With the British foreign secretary Salisbury he renewed the Chinese laborer treaty.
translations.idiomatic: He renegotiated the Chinese labor treaty with British foreign secretary Lord Salisbury.

sentences.zh: 歷通政使副使、左副都御史，留使如故。

translations.literal: He passed through vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission and left vice censor-in-chief, remaining envoy as before.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission and left vice censor-in-chief while keeping his diplomatic post.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調使俄奧和三國。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred as envoy to Russia, Austria, and the three states.
translations.idiomatic: In 1896 he was reassigned as envoy to Russia and Austria-Hungary.

sentences.zh: 越二年，晉工部侍郎，仍駐俄。

translations.literal: After two years he was promoted to vice minister of works, still stationed in Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to vice minister of works while remaining in Russia.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳亂作，聯軍入津沽，電命儒遞國書，乞俄調解。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer turmoil arose; the allied armies entered Taku; by telegram Ru was ordered to present a state letter and beg Russian mediation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the Boxers rose and allied forces took Taku, Yang Ru was telegraphed to present credentials and ask Russia to mediate.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，車駕幸西安。

translations.literal: The capital fell and the imperial carriage proceeded to Xi’an.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing fell and the court fled to Xi’an.

sentences.zh: 俄佯議撤兵，而潛使人詣關東，掠吉林、黑龍江地，達營口北。

translations.literal: Russia pretended to discuss troop withdrawal but secretly sent men to Guandong, seizing lands in Jilin and Heilongjiang as far north as Yingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Russia feigned willingness to withdraw troops while secretly occupying Jilin and Heilongjiang and advancing to north of Yingkou.

sentences.zh: 儒至黑海行宮與婉商，俄允還地，而不允撤保路兵。

translations.literal: Ru went to the Black Sea palace for tactful negotiation; Russia agreed to return territory but would not withdraw railway-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the Black Sea summer palace Ru negotiated delicately; Russia promised to return land but refused to pull back railway guards.

sentences.zh: 將軍增祺遽與訂密約九款，多失權利，上責其謬妄，下嚴旨，仍令儒與俄議。

translations.literal: General Zeng Qi hastily concluded a secret treaty of nine articles, losing many rights; the emperor rebuked his absurdity and issued a stern edict, still ordering Ru to negotiate with Russia.
translations.idiomatic: General Zeng Qi rashly signed a secret nine-article pact conceding far too much. The throne rebuked him and ordered Yang Ru to continue negotiations with Russia.

sentences.zh: 儒與商更約，俄堅拒，儒正色曰：「既言保我自主，何兵權、利權、命官權而不予畀？

translations.literal: Ru negotiated to revise the treaty; Russia firmly refused. Ru said sternly: "Since you speak of preserving our autonomy, why not grant military authority, economic rights, and the power to appoint officials?
translations.idiomatic: When Russia refused to revise the treaty, Ru said firmly: "You claim to protect our sovereignty—why then withhold military, economic, and appointive powers?

sentences.zh: 既稱不利土地，何以東三省不為中國版圖？」

translations.literal: Since you say you do not desire our land, why are the three eastern provinces not on China’s map?"
translations.idiomatic: If you want no territory, why treat the three eastern provinces as if they were not Chinese soil?"

sentences.zh: 俄窮於應，始允別立正約。

translations.literal: Russia, at a loss for reply, finally agreed to draw up a formal treaty separately.
translations.idiomatic: Russia, unable to answer, finally agreed to negotiate a proper treaty.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，授為全權大臣。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended this, appointing him plenipotentiary minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his stand and made him plenipotentiary.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，俄交草約十二款，趣畫押。

translations.literal: After more than a year Russia presented a draft treaty of twelve articles and urged signature.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Russia submitted a twelve-article draft and pressed for signature.

sentences.zh: 東南士民甚激昂，各國亦騰口舌，朝旨命再商改。

translations.literal: Southeastern scholars and people were greatly agitated; various states also raised clamor; a court edict ordered further negotiation for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage swept the southeast; foreign powers protested as well; the court ordered further revision.

sentences.zh: 儒責其外部食言，語激切，俄人勉為改數事，而仍未平準。

translations.literal: Ru reproached their foreign ministry for breaking faith, his words fierce; the Russians reluctantly changed several items, yet still did not balance the terms.
translations.idiomatic: Ru accused the foreign ministry of bad faith in heated language; Russia grudgingly altered a few clauses but the terms remained unfair.

sentences.zh: 儒數往謁，拒不見，見則第趣畫諾，語竟即起，不容儒致一詞。

translations.literal: Ru went several times to call; they refused to see him; when they did see him they only urged approval, and when words ended they rose at once, not allowing Ru to speak a single further phrase.
translations.idiomatic: Ru called repeatedly but was often refused audience; when received, Russians only demanded his assent and dismissed him before he could speak.

sentences.zh: 儒憤出，及階踣，傷右足，乞假赴德、奧療治。

translations.literal: Ru left in anger; on the steps he fell and injured his right foot; he begged leave to go to Germany and Austria for treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving in fury, he fell on the steps and broke his right foot; he took leave to seek treatment in Germany and Austria.

sentences.zh: 俄留之，且因其病篤，命駐華公使戢耳詩與李鴻章在京協定。

translations.literal: Russia detained him, and because his illness was grave ordered the minister to China Giers and Li Hongzhang in the capital to conclude the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Russia kept him in place; citing his grave illness, it had minister Giers and Li Hongzhang finalize terms in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 儒復請代，不許。

translations.literal: Ru again requested a replacement; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again to be replaced; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 調戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，卒，予優恤。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he died; generous condolence gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following first month; the court granted generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中國遣使，始於光緒初。

translations.literal: The commentary says: China’s dispatch of envoys began at the beginning of Guangxu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: China began sending permanent envoys in the early Guangxu era.

sentences.zh: 嵩燾首膺其選，論交涉獨具遠識。

translations.literal: Songshen was first chosen; in discussing foreign relations he alone possessed far-sighted judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Songshen was the first chosen; on diplomacy he alone showed true foresight.

sentences.zh: 崇厚擅定俄約，誤國甚矣。

translations.literal: Chonghou on his own authority fixed the Russian treaty—a grave harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou’s unauthorized Russian treaty did grave harm to the nation.

sentences.zh: 紀澤繼之，抗議改正。

translations.literal: Jize succeeded him and protested to secure revision.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize followed and fought to revise it.

sentences.zh: 其時國勢猶足自申焉。

translations.literal: At that time national strength was still sufficient to assert itself.
translations.idiomatic: China’s strength still allowed some self-assertion then.

sentences.zh: 至儒爭密約，竟以憤死，終不能挽救，公理尚可恃乎？

translations.literal: When it came to Ru’s struggle over the secret treaty, he died of indignation in the end and could not rescue the situation—can impartial principle still be relied upon?
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ru fought the secret Manchurian pact, he died of outrage without saving the day—can justice still be counted on?

sentences.zh: 福成、庶昌諸人，並嫺文學，各有著述，討論修飾，皆美使才也。

translations.literal: Fucheng, Shuchang, and the others were all skilled in letters, each with writings; in discussion and polish they were all fine envoy talents.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fucheng, Li Shuchang, and others were all accomplished writers with published works—polished minds and fine envoy material.

sentences.zh: 馬建忠定亂濟變，策奇制勝，亦有足多，故並附於篇。

translations.literal: Ma Jianzhong settled turmoil and managed crises; his stratagems were singular and victorious—he too has much to commend, and therefore all are appended in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jianzhong quelled disorder with brilliant expedients worthy of praise, and so they are all included in this chapter.
